entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof development of reduction idea toward NP-hardness of feature selection for relative Gaussian c-separation in the formulation of Borozan et al. The argument starts from NP-completeness of equal-cardinality partition of positive squares, giving integral Gaussian data via integer roots and an even paired total. Three Gaussians enforce partition balance, and a schedule of d+1 Gaussians enforces binary selectors. Explicit separation of the two blocks makes cross-block hinge penalties vanish. The fixed threshold is (dot s 1 / 2)*d*(d+1)/2 - 3*d/4, an integer multiple of 1/4 for natural input weights. Here d is the full dimension. The main proved result is the pointwise gadget iff. The full complexity reduction is not formalized. The threshold depends only on the input. General Karamata inequality and an unconditional ordinary-PARTITION to perfect-square equal-cardinality partition equivalence are auxiliary results stated in Solution.lean. The square encoding has proved injectivity and numerical size bounds; its NP-completeness argument is documented prose. The original Gaussian gadget predicate also has a proved binary certificate verifier with soundness, completeness, and quadratic work in a bit-cost model. The Gaussian gadget equivalence and square-partition reduction were developed and first presented by the author in this formalization. Their mathematical novelty and priority relative to earlier literature are unknown; no systematic literature search or comparison establishing them has been documented.
entries.title: NP-hardness of Gaussian c-separation

entries.abstract: Lean 4 results (core Lean, no dependencies, no axioms beyond the standard three) about law 1518 of the Equational Theories Project, x = (y ◇ y) ◇ (x ◇ (y ◇ x)). Theorem A: in every magma satisfying 1518 and 3862 (x ◇ x = (x ◇ (x ◇ x)) ◇ x), writing S x = x ◇ x, the set {x, S x, S (S x)} is closed under ◇ with u ◇ v = S v and S (S (S x)) = x; hence every one-generated such magma is the trivial magma or the three-element cyclic shift x ◇ y = y + 1. This proves a classification conjectured by Terence Tao on the Lean Zulip on 2024-11-29 (message 485148288). That message assumed 1518 together with all four of 47, 614, 817 and 3862 and carried no finiteness hypothesis; assuming 3862 alone is no weaker, because Matthew Bolan reported the same day (message 485153888) that 1518 and 3862 already imply the other three. What is added here is a machine-checked proof, not a weaker hypothesis: no proof of the classification was found in the venues searched. Theorem A is what the compared declarations state. Outside them the repository holds an explicit family of finite 1518-magmas that do violate the four targets, with two members checked by kernel evaluation, and kernel-checked certificate identities behind a cohomological obstruction theorem (every 1518-cocycle over the shift with finite fibre is a coboundary), whose reduction is a written proof, and the computations classifying base-dependent extensions of the shift.
entries.title: One-generated (1518 + 3862)-magmas are trivial or the Z/3 shift; an explicit family of finite 1518-magmas violating laws 47, 614, 817, 3862

entries.abstract: A Lean proof resolving the Burr–Erdős–Graham–Sós conjecture (Erdős Problem 809): for every fixed odd cycle of length at least seven, the maximal anti-Ramsey threshold at floor(n²/4) + 1 edges is n²/8 + o(n²). The seven-cycle case is new to our knowledge. The development proves it and formalizes the stronger full-density result of Bucić, Chen, and Ma for odd cycles of length at least nine.
entries.title: Erdős Problem 809: rainbow odd cycles

entries.abstract: Erdős problem #1219 (erdosproblems.com/1219; Erdős–Hajnal 1971, Problem 3, asked by Erdős, Hajnal and Rado): let (n_k) be an increasing sequence of integers such that 2^{ℵ_{n_k}} is strictly increasing and 2^{ℵ_{n_0}} > ℵ_ω; is it true that Σ_k 2^{ℵ_{n_k}} → (ℵ_ω)²?  Shelah (Notes on partition calculus, 1975, §1) proved that the answer is yes.  This project formalizes that proof in Lean 4 with Mathlib: the comparator target erdos_1219 states that for every strictly increasing n : ℕ → ℕ with k ↦ 2 ^ ℵ_(n k) strictly increasing and ℵ_ω < 2 ^ ℵ_(n 0), the binary partition relation PartitionArrow (Σ_k 2 ^ ℵ_(n k)) ℵ_ω holds, i.e. every 2-colouring of the 2-element subsets of a set of cardinality Σ_k 2 ^ ℵ_(n k) has a monochromatic subset of cardinality ℵ_ω (PartitionArrow is the binary case of formal-conjectures' Combinatorics.cardinalPartitionRel).  The proof follows Shelah's Canonization Lemma 1.1 and Theorem 1.2: the unbalanced Erdős–Rado theorem (2^μ)⁺ → ((2^μ)⁺, μ⁺)² (proved here with a critical-ordinal / closure-point argument), a canonization of the colouring across blocks of sizes (2^{ℵ_{n_k}})⁺ by means of guides generic over all small subsets of the earlier blocks, and Ramsey's theorem for pairs on ℕ.  The target is proved from propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only and passes the Lean comparator (landrun sandbox, NanoDa kernel).
entries.title: Erdős Problem #1219 in Lean 4: Σ_k 2^{ℵ_{n_k}} → (ℵ_ω)² (Shelah 1975)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 characterization of two-fold Langford sequences. An m-fold Langford sequence of order l and defect d fills the positions 1, ..., 2ml so that every p in [d, d + l - 1] occupies the endpoints of m pairwise disjoint pairs of positions at distance p. For d, l >= 1 a two-fold sequence exists exactly when 3l >= 2d - 1. For every m, (2m - 1)l >= 2d - 1 is necessary, with l(2d + l + 1) = 0 (mod 4) for odd m, and the bound is attained whenever 2d + l = 2ml + 1; the row of order one exists exactly when d divides m; no three-fold sequence of order 3 and defect 6 exists; and for every m >= 3 the necessary conditions are not sufficient. For every T >= 1, with r = ml mod T, every m-fold sequence satisfies the residue bound r(T - r) <= m * sum |p - T| over p in [d, d + l - 1], which contains the counting bound and the necessity half of the order-one theorem. Every m-fold sequence satisfies the forced-endpoint bound 6mld + ml <= 4d^2 + 2(ml)^2 + ml^2. For every m >= 3 the cell (d, l) = (3m - 3, 3) meets the necessary conditions and admits no m-fold sequence. Equality 2d + l = 2ml + 1 holds exactly when every pair straddles the middle, that is ml < i + s_i for every position i <= ml. Alkasasbeh, Dyer and Howell define these sequences and ask for necessary and sufficient conditions when m >= 2; this repository answers the question for m = 2. Necessity is a distance sum. Sufficiency at m = 2 is strong induction on l: sixteen literal cells, concatenation, and otherwise a mirror-symmetric sequence built by Lemma S from a signed permutation, which is found on the whole cone by inversion, the reversal, a descent along lines of fixed mu, and in the band by 21 block-reversal families plus the two-block reversal tau_l, eight sporadic cells and three bases. The tight line is m interleaved copies of the source's Table 1.
entries.title: Two-fold Langford sequences exist exactly when 3l ≥ 2d − 1; the m-fold counting bound and its attainment, and a residue bound

entries.abstract: We answer the set-theoretic characterization question for digraph support families posed by Mike Steel in Section 4 of Interior operators and their relationship to autocatalytic networks (arXiv:2305.16714v4, 2023). A digraph on a finite set E is given by a predecessor map P assigning to each vertex e a set P(e) of in-neighbours, loops allowed, and a set S is supported when every element e of S has some element of S in P(e). The characterization refers only to the family F. Start from the full power set of E with no roots used. A legal step chooses a remaining set S outside F that is inclusion-maximal among the remaining sets outside F, chooses a root r in S that has not been used before and lies in no member of F contained in S, and deletes every remaining set X with r in X and X contained in S. A family F of subsets of E is exactly the support family of some predecessor map on E if and only if some finite sequence of legal steps ends exactly at F.
entries.title: Characterizing digraph support families by rooted-interval deletion

entries.abstract: A formalization in Lean 4 and Mathlib of the Erdős discrepancy theorem, proved by Terence Tao in 2015: for every sequence f(1), f(2), … of signs ±1 and every C there are d ≥ 1 and n with |f(d) + f(2d) + ⋯ + f(nd)| > C, so every ±1 sequence has unbounded discrepancy along homogeneous arithmetic progressions. This is the original ±1 formulation, Corollary 1.2 of Tao's paper; its Hilbert-space-valued Theorem 1.1 is not formalized. The proof follows the architecture of Tao's argument: a Fourier-analytic reduction from a sequence of bounded discrepancy to a stochastic completely multiplicative function with bounded mean-square partial sums; a van der Corput argument, driven by the logarithmically averaged two-point Elliott estimate, forcing such a function to pretend to be a twisted Dirichlet character; and a generalized Borwein–Choi–Coons argument excluding that case. The analytic number theory these steps use is proved in the same development rather than assumed: the entropy-decrement proof of the two-point Elliott estimate from Tao's companion paper, the Matomäki–Radziwiłł short-interval estimate on the major arcs via the Dirichlet-polynomial route of Matomäki, Radziwiłł and Tao, the Halász–Montgomery large-values inequality, a large-values bound for Dirichlet polynomials over primes from a zero-free region of the Riemann zeta function, that zero-free region from Weyl-sum bounds on zeta, and a form of Vinogradov's mean value theorem. Where a published route did not fit, the development adapts it; the adaptations are documented. The theorem depends only on Lean's three standard axioms. This is a formalization of a published result, not a new proof; it was produced by AI agents working through pull requests checked by continuous integration in the ProofFleet repository (formerly MoltResearch).
entries.title: A Lean formalization of the Erdős discrepancy theorem

entries.abstract: Lean proofs of strong duality and exact block composition for the negative-weight adversary bound on total Boolean functions, explicit constant-factor characterizations of bounded-error quantum query complexity in value and Boolean XOR oracle models, and uniform extraction of query algorithms from supplied promise dual certificates. The submission also proves that every output probability of a q-query algorithm on Boolean inputs has a real polynomial representation of degree at most 2q in each model. Seven statements are compared against a standalone Mathlib-only specification of the finite quantum model.
entries.title: Adversary bounds and the polynomial method for quantum queries

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of the implication from five explicitly stated literature inputs to a homeomorphism between the ordinary Gromov--Hausdorff space of nonempty compact metric spaces and real square-summable sequences. The proof constructs invariant full-support probability assignments, finite dimensional local models, global AR domination and discrete approximation. The five literature inputs are assumptions, not theorems proved in this snapshot.
entries.title: Conditional Hilbert-space classification of Gromov--Hausdorff space

entries.abstract: Formalization in Lean 4 / mathlib of the existing paper by Furber, Mardare, Panangaden, and Scott, Interpreting Lambda Calculus in Domain-Valued Random Variables (LIPIcs, Vol. 363, CSL 2026, Article 48). This repository formalizes that published mathematics; it does not present the paper's results as new mathematics originating in this repository. Three capstones sit on top of the rest of the paper: Theorem 26 (internal λ-interpretation in SetoidF_A), Corollary 34 (the Engeler model with numerals in V^A), and Theorem 43 (two fair-coin subsets of ℕ that are incomparable under the λ-definable many-one preorder). Domain-theory background is imported from a vendored copy of scott1972. The Palomar Challenge locks Theorem 43 as csl2026 and proposition_36_i on the Engeler graph model. Full Corollary 34 remains kernel-checked in the library and is not represented by a weaker Mathlib-only proxy. Lean is written by AI agents under the direction and review of the author. Dana Scott gave the author the paper. This formalization does not claim that the paper's authors participated in it or endorsed it. There is no sorry outside the deliberate holes in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, and Mathlib is the only Lake require.
entries.title: Lean Formalization of Interpreting Lambda Calculus in Domain-Valued Random Variables (CSL 2026)

entries.abstract: For every finite abelian extension L/K of a nonarchimedean local field, the multiplicative group K× modulo the field-norm subgroup N_{L/K}(L×) is isomorphic as a topological group to Gal(L/K). The registered declaration is the finite norm-quotient form of local reciprocity proved in the included ClassFieldTheory development. Stronger compatibility, normalization and existence results in that development are documented separately and are not part of the compared declaration.
entries.title: Local class field theory in Lean 4.35.0-rc2

entries.abstract: For every finite abelian extension L/K of number fields, the idèle class group C_K modulo the image of the idèle-class norm from C_L is isomorphic as a topological multiplicative group to Gal(L/K). The Challenge defines the norm as the determinant on the relative adèle algebra and descends it through principal idèles; the included ClassFieldTheory development supplies the proof of the resulting reciprocity theorem.
entries.title: Global class field theory in Lean 4.35.0-rc2

entries.abstract: Glauberman and Norton (Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 119, 1993) end their paper on a combinatorial problem that arises in the proof of the Feit–Thompson odd order theorem with a question of Péterfalvi: can the hypothesis of their Proposition 9 be satisfied for p = 3? The same question is Problem 1 in Appendix C of Bender and Glauberman, Local Analysis for the Odd Order Theorem (1994). Let F be the field with p^q elements, P its additive group, U its group of units of norm one over the prime field, H the semidirect product P ⋊ U, and P₀ the image of the additive group of the prime field in H. Hypothesis (B) asks for an injective homomorphism σ from H into a group G, a finite abelian subgroup Q of G whose order is prime to p, and an element y of Q, such that σ(P₀) normalizes Q and σ(P₀)^y normalizes σ(U). Proposition 9 also assumes condition (A): q does not divide p − 1. This project proves in Lean 4 that the answer is negative: for every prime q with q ∤ 3 − 1, no group G, finite or infinite, satisfies hypothesis (B) with p = 3. It also proves Péterfalvi's example from the same paper, which shows that SL(2, 2^q) satisfies hypothesis (B) with p = 2, so the hypothesis is not empty. The proof is new. It turns a witness of hypothesis (B) into relations between three copies of the additive group of the field with 3^q elements, and it rules out these relations by arithmetic in that field.
entries.title: Péterfalvi's Problem for p = 3: No Group Satisfies Hypothesis (B)

entries.abstract:
A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the Four Color Theorem, ported from Georges Gonthier's Coq proof by Claude Opus 5.5, Anthropic's AI model, working as an agent under the direction of Robert D. Barish. The main theorem, FourColor.RealPlane.four_color, states that every simple map of the real plane can be colored with at most four colors so that adjacent regions get different colors. The map may have infinitely many regions, bounded or not; each region must be open and connected, and two regions are adjacent when their closures share a point that lies in the closure of no third region. As in Coq, a compactness argument reduces the theorem to finite maps, which are turned into planar bridgeless hypermaps. A smallest hypermap that cannot be four-colored cannot exist: discharging shows that it would contain one of the 633 configurations of Robertson, Sanders, Seymour and Thomas, and each of these is reducible.
The port differs from the Coq proof in three main ways. Its statement uses Mathlib's real numbers rather than an arbitrary model of Coq's axiomatized reals; the two are equivalent, because all such models are isomorphic and the definitions use only the order. Coq checks that the 633 configurations are reducible with a procedure on trees of colorings, run by its virtual machine. The port replaces it with a new bit-parallel engine whose certificates, generated during the build, are checked by the Lean kernel itself. Finally, the case analysis of the unavoidability proof, written as tactic scripts in Coq, becomes case trees checked by a checker proved correct once. Every computation is carried out by the Lean kernel, without native_decide, and the proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: The Four Color Theorem (Lean 4 port of Gonthier's Coq proof)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof that the zero-forcing number of the generalized Petersen graph P(n,3) is exactly 8 for every natural number n >= 13. The formalized result is the statement recorded as Conjecture 5 in Arnav Krishnan's July 2026 correction preprint; this repository supplies and kernel-checks a proof of that conjectured statement rather than formalizing a proof already given in the cited preprint.
entries.title: Zero forcing number of the generalized Petersen graphs P(n,3)

entries.abstract: In a catalytic reaction system with finitely many reactions, a RAF is a nonempty set of reactions whose reactants are produced from the food set by iterated closure under the selected reactions and whose reactions are each catalysed by a molecule of that closure. Steel (arXiv:2305.16714v4, Section 4) asked whether some reaction always lies in at least half of the RAFs. Call a reaction food-ready if all its reactants are food, and abundant if it lies in at least half of the sets in the family formed by the RAFs and the empty set. If some RAF U consists entirely of food-ready reactions, then some reaction of U is abundant, with no condition on the other reactions. If every reaction of the system, except at most two, is food-ready and the system has a RAF, then some reaction is abundant. Finally, the statement that every catalytic reaction system with finitely many reactions and a RAF has an abundant reaction is equivalent to Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture in the form: every finite union-closed family containing the empty set and a nonempty set has an element lying in at least half of its members.
entries.title: Equivalence of the RAF abundance conjecture and Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the whole of P. Corvaja and U. Zannier, On the rational approximations to the powers of an algebraic number: solution of two problems of Mahler and Mendès France (Acta Math. 193 (2004)), built on the repository's libraries ArithmeticHeights and DiophantineApproximation, whose Subspace Theorem it uses. The library CorvajaZannier2004 is sorry-free and within Lean's three standard axioms. It proves the Main Theorem (finitely many non-pseudo-Pisot δqu that are very close to integers, u in a finitely generated group of algebraic numbers), Theorem 1 (Mahler's question: if ‖αⁿ‖ < lⁿ infinitely often, some power of α is a Pisot number), Lemmas 1–5, Theorem 2 (Mendès France's question: the period of the continued fraction of αⁿ tends to infinity unless α is a unit or a square root of a rational, and is bounded for units), and the Appendix (the word "algebraic" cannot be dropped from Theorem 1). Eleven statements are compared.
entries.title: Corvaja–Zannier 2004: rational approximations to the powers of an algebraic number

entries.abstract: We prove uniform cancellation in prime-weighted exponential sums at the 2/15 scale, improving the 8/33 local Fourier scale in the Matomäki–Radziwiłł–Tao machinery for averaged prime-pair correlations. On the minor-arc part of every centered arc of radius 1/(2H), the squared von Mangoldt exponential sum over X < n <= 2X has integral at most C X (log X)^(-A), for every A > 0 and epsilon > 0, once H >= X^(2/15+epsilon) and X is large enough. The center may lie anywhere on the circle. The same cutoffs and constants work for every center and are chosen before X and H. This gives uniform minor-arc cancellation at the 2/15 threshold. Since 2/15 < 8/33, the admissible H is smaller, so the frequency windows of length 1/H are wider and the shift-averaging intervals are shorter. The constants C and X0 are ineffective because the proof uses Siegel's theorem. The development also contains an internal proof of the epsilon-form of Guth–Maynard's large-value estimate for Dirichlet polynomials. The recorded 20 September Lean 4.30 kernel replays checked 100,596 declarations for MAP and 75,874 for Guth–Maynard, using only standard axioms. The formal statement is AllCenterMAP.map_two_fifteenths, manuscript Theorem 1.1.
entries.title: Uniform Minor-Arc Cancellation for Primes at the X^{2/15+ε} Scale

entries.abstract: Lean proofs that every metric TSP instance on at least three vertices has a Hamiltonian tour costing at most (3/2 - 2.05522e-30) times any feasible subtour-LP objective, with one strictly larger saving uniform over all instances. The submission also exposes the exact finite-layer saving and a KKO-framework bound using GKL capacity estimates.
entries.title: Metric TSP subtour-LP integrality gap

entries.abstract: This project formalizes the existence of a model companion for the first-order theory of groups satisfying x^3 = 1. Its principal group-theoretic result gives a uniform, explicit bound on the number of generators needed to witness a failure of amalgamation with an existentially closed exponent-three group. The development follows the accompanying manuscript through free groups, associated graded Lie algebras, strict extensions, and the bounded-amalgamation criterion.
entries.title: Existence of a Model Companion for Groups of Exponent 3: Lean Formalization

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the following theorem: there are absolute constants C, n0 > 0 such that every connected Cayley graph Cay(G, S) on n >= n0 vertices whose degree d = |S| is at least C (log n)^13 / log log n contains a Hamilton cycle (Lovasz.hamiltonian_of_polylog_degree). Here G is a finite group, S is a connection set (S = S^-1 and 1 not in S, so the graph is |S|-regular), log is the natural logarithm, and connectivity is equivalent to S generating G. The theorem is a case of the Lovász conjecture (every connected vertex-transitive graph has a Hamilton path) in its Cayley-graph form (every connected Cayley graph on at least three vertices is Hamiltonian). For arbitrary connected Cayley graphs the previously published degree thresholds were linear degree (Christofides, Hladký and Máthé, 2014) and degree at least n^(1-c) (Bedert, Draganić, Müyesser and Pavez-Signé, 2026). The proof follows the source manuscript: it extracts a connected bipartite template with spectral gap of order (log n)^-2, allocates the vertices to weighted translates of the template by signed rounding (a robust signed integrality theorem derived from the capacitated b-matching polytope, swap rounding, and a trace-exponential matrix concentration bound), connects the pieces by a sparse matching chosen by mutual nominations and a signed circulation, absorbs the outside matching inside every piece with Hamilton routers built from even-cycle comparators, and merges cycles. Every lemma of the manuscript is proved in the repository, as are the classical results it uses without proof (normalized Cheeger inequality, Haxell's hypergraph matching theorem, the b-matching polytope, Watkins's connectivity bound, the Nash-Williams–Tutte tree-packing theorem, Hoffman's circulation criterion, scalar Chernoff bounds); Hall's theorem is taken from Mathlib, and matrix Bernstein is avoided by deriving the one lemma that used it from the manuscript's own concentration bound. The source manuscript is an unpublished research draft that describes its own proof as not independently verified; this formalization is, to the maintainer's knowledge, the first verification of the theorem. The proved theorem has no sorry and depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: Hamilton cycles in Cayley graphs of polylogarithmic degree

entries.abstract: Formalizes the continuous-type bilateral-trade impossibility result: no mechanism can satisfy ex post efficiency (almost surely), Bayesian incentive compatibility, interim individual rationality, and weak ex ante budget balance when buyer and seller supports overlap. The proof uses payoff equivalence and envelope identities, together with the strict rent-gap identity B + C > S.
entries.title: Myerson-Satterthwaite impossibility theorem (continuous bilateral-trade version)

entries.abstract: Erdős problem #1220 (erdosproblems.com/1220; Erdős–Hajnal 1971): let λ be a singular cardinal such that both λ and cf(λ) are ℵ₀-inaccessible (μ^ℵ₀ < κ for all μ < κ); does λ → (λ, ℵ₁)² hold?  This formalization settles the question as asked on erdosproblems.com in the negative sense "not provable": ZFC does not prove that every such λ satisfies λ → (λ, ℵ₁)² (erdos1220_not_provable : ¬ (ZFC ⊨ᵇ Erdos1220)), i.e. there is a model of ZFC with a singular λ, λ and cf(λ) ℵ₀-inaccessible, and λ ↛ (λ, ℵ₁)².  Shelah and Stanley (Sh:258, Ann. Pure Appl. Logic 36 (1987)) showed that a negative answer is consistent with ZFC.  This project formalizes that consistency result: the comparator target erdos1220_not_provable : ¬ (ZFC ⊨ᵇ Erdos1220) is stated for literally the same first-order theory ZFC, language and ZFSet interpretation as elliotglazer/erdos501's comparator challenge (imported from its statement module Erdos501.FOL.Statement), together with a faithfulness theorem erdos1220_sentence_faithful: in Mathlib's ZFSet the sentence Erdos1220 holds iff the Mathlib-level statement Erdos1220.Problem1220 holds.  The witness is the ground-model singular strong-limit cardinal λ = ℶ_{𝔠⁺} (cf λ = 𝔠⁺; λ and cf λ are ℵ₀-inaccessible without any deep cardinal-arithmetic input), not ℵ_{𝔠⁺}.  The forcing is the Shelah–Stanley §3 forcing, formalized as block-preserving, block-covering histories of basic conditions (weak extension order), with the μ⁺-strategic closure (hence μ-distributivity) and the (2^μ)⁺-chain condition proved in ZFC without GCH (Δ-system lemma for (2^μ)⁺ sets of size ≤ μ, blueprint counting (2^μ)^μ = 2^μ).  In the Boolean-valued model of its regular-open algebra (built with the Lean 4 port of Han–van Doorn's Flypitch vendored by erdos501) the hypotheses on λ are preserved, the generic colouring of [λ]² has neither a red homogeneous set of size λ nor a blue homogeneous set of size ℵ₁, and Flypitch's completeness theorem turns this into a two-valued model of ZFC satisfying ¬Erdos1220.  Both targets are proved from propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only and pass the Lean comparator.  Only the negative direction is claimed: independence (consistency of a positive answer) is NOT claimed.
entries.title: Erdős Problem #1220 in Lean 4: the affirmative statement is not provable in ZFC

entries.abstract: Formalizes the Gibbard-Satterthwaite theorem for finite electorates and finite alternative sets with at least three alternatives: every onto, strategy-proof social choice function is dictatorial. The proof constructs a social welfare function and reduces to Arrow's impossibility theorem.
entries.title: Gibbard-Satterthwaite theorem (strategy-proof social choice)

entries.abstract: We establish three sets of results addressing published questions about the composition, enumeration and degradation of autocatalytic reaction networks. In response to the composition questions of Gagrani, Wang, De Decker and Lacoste (arXiv:2603.02627, Discussion and outlook), we give exact criteria for strict increases in the maximum amplification factor (MAF) under reaction addition, nonnegative species aggregation and shared-species coupling, assuming nonnegative inputs and attained MAFs. A block direct sum attains the larger component MAF, while an explicit example shows that component MAFs alone do not determine the MAF of a coupled network. Addressing the CS-core enumeration direction of Golnik, Gatter, Stadler and Vassena (arXiv:2603.02770, Section 6), we prove exact reconstruction from a complete list of ordinary-core anchor matchings, each unique on its vertex set, by alternating-path generation and certified rational semipositivity filtering. We establish existence of the certified test, its rejection of the empty matching, and an explicit nonempty instance for A → 2A. For the arbitrary-degradation question discussed by Nandan, Nghe and Unterberger (arXiv:2507.15546, Section 6), we characterize growth, criticality and extinction for irreducible linear diluted source networks with nonnegative unary reaction data and species degradation d ≥ 0: the real spectral bound of A − diag(d) is positive, zero or negative exactly when d is componentwise strictly below, equal to or strictly above (Av)_i/v_i for some positive v. We also characterize partial-actuation stabilizability of Metzler matrices through a positive-vector certificate on the unactuated block. All eleven selected statements are formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib.
entries.title: MAF composition criteria, exact enumeration of child-selection autocatalytic cores, and degradation regions of linear diluted source networks

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof that at least one of the 2-adic zeta values ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9) is irrational. The theorem has no hypotheses, and its proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The values are defined through the Volkenborn integral: zeta2 s = J(s−1)/((s−1)·2^s), where J(s) is the 2-adic limit of the Riemann sums 2^(−N) Σ_{x<2^N} (x+1/2)^(−s), and the theorem also proves that these limits exist. By Lemma 2.8 of Lai, Sprang and Zudilin (IMRN 2026), zeta2 s is the Kubota–Leopoldt value ζ₂(s) = L₂(s, ω^(1−s)) for s ≥ 2. That identification is cited, not formalised; it only involves a non-zero rational factor, which does not affect irrationality. The result sharpens Theorem 1.1 (case s = 3) of L. Lai (Int. J. Number Theory 2025), which shows that at least one of ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11), ζ₂(13) is irrational, and it implies the companion result, formalised in a separate repository, that at least one of ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11) is irrational. The proof uses linear forms S_n = ∫ R_n'''(t+1/2) dt in 1, ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9) built from the shifted well-poised rational functions R_n(t) = (2t+n) Π_{m=1}^{6} (t+1/2−h_m)_(n+2h_m) / (t)_(n+1)^6 with h = (n/40)(−17, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6). The 2-adic size of S_n comes from Lai's and Sprang's Δ-calculus. The size of the coefficients comes from a contour-integral representation and a saddle-point bound, whose numerical inequalities are certified in Lean. The odd part of the denominators is bounded by Legendre-type counts at the poles, the vanishing of R_n at half-integers, kernel-checked certificates and the prime number theorem (proved here from a vendored Lean proof of the Wiener–Ikehara theorem). If both values were rational, the valuations of the coefficients at the prime n − 1 (an idea of Lai and Sprang) would make S_n non-zero for infinitely many n, and Lai's irrationality criterion gives the contradiction. The mathematics and the Lean code were produced by AI agents under human direction and have not been refereed.
entries.title: At least one of the 2-adic zeta values ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9) is irrational

entries.abstract: Addressing the RAF-realizability question in Section 4 of Mike Steel's Interior Operators and Their Relationship to Autocatalytic Networks (arXiv:2305.16714v4, 2023), we characterize which interior operators on the subsets of a finite set E are maxRAF operators of catalytic reaction systems whose reaction set is exactly E. An interior operator is represented by its family of fixed sets, a union-closed family containing the empty set. A same-ground realization is a system with one reaction per element of E, finitely many molecule types, a food set and a catalysis relation; it realizes the empty set together with its RAFs, the nonempty reaction sets whose reactants arise from food by iterated closure under the selected reactions and whose reactions are each catalysed by a molecule of that closure. Such a family has a same-ground realization if and only if it is the intersection of an accessible union-closed family A and a predecessor-support family. Here A contains the empty set, is closed under unions, and every nonempty member of A has an element whose removal leaves a member of A; the members of A need not cover E. A set S is supported by a predecessor map P on E when every element e of S has some element of S in P(e), loops allowed. The family consisting of the empty set and all subsets of size at least three has a same-ground realization if and only if E has at most four elements. This gives the sharp threshold for the family considered in Proposition 5 and its subsequent remarks in Steel (2023). Both results are formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib.
entries.title: Same-ground RAF realizability of finite interior operators and the four-reaction threshold for the empty-or-at-least-three family

entries.abstract: Formalizes Arrow's impossibility theorem for finitely many voters and finitely many alternatives (at least three): every social welfare function satisfying unanimity and independence of irrelevant alternatives is dictatorial. The proof follows the classical decisive-coalition argument: field expansion (a coalition decisive for one pair is decisive for every pair) and group contraction (a decisive coalition with at least two voters contains a smaller decisive coalition), iterated down to a singleton dictator. This is a reusable formalization artifact, not a claim of new mathematics.
entries.title: Arrow's impossibility theorem (general finite version)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof that at least one of the 2-adic zeta values ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11) is irrational. The theorem has no hypotheses, and its proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The values are defined through the Volkenborn integral: zeta2 s = J(s−1)/((s−1)·2^s), where J(s) is the 2-adic limit of the Riemann sums 2^(−N) Σ_{x<2^N} (x+1/2)^(−s), and the theorem also proves that these limits exist. By Lemma 2.8 of Lai, Sprang and Zudilin (IMRN 2026), zeta2 s is the Kubota–Leopoldt value ζ₂(s) = L₂(s, ω^(1−s)) for s ≥ 2. That identification is cited, not formalised; it only involves a non-zero rational factor, which does not affect irrationality. The result sharpens Theorem 1.1 (case s = 3) of L. Lai (Int. J. Number Theory 2025), which shows that at least one of ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11), ζ₂(13) is irrational. The proof uses linear forms S_n = −∫ R_n'''(t+1/2) dt in 1, ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11), with R_n(t) = 2^(16n)(2t+n)(t+1/2)_n^8/(t)_(n+1)^8. Their denominators are controlled by a one-power saving that comes from Andrews' multiple-series transformation (proved here in Lean) and by the prime number theorem (proved here from a vendored Lean proof of the Wiener–Ikehara theorem). The exact 2-adic valuation of S_n along n = 2^m − 1 shows that S_n ≠ 0, and Lai's irrationality criterion concludes. The mathematics and the Lean code were produced by AI agents under human direction and have not been refereed.
entries.title: At least one of the 2-adic zeta values ζ₂(7), ζ₂(9), ζ₂(11) is irrational

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of Schmidt's Subspace Theorem and the theory beneath it, following Bombieri–Gubler, Heights in Diophantine Geometry (Chapters 1–7), and Schmidt's route in general. Two libraries, sorry-free and within Lean's three standard axioms. ArithmeticHeights builds heights of points, polynomials, matrices and linear subspaces, Northcott and Kronecker, Minkowski's second theorem, Siegel's lemma and the Bombieri–Vaaler theorems. DiophantineApproximation builds on it Roth's theorem over a number field with several places (and Ridout, the p-adic form, targets at infinity, moving targets), the geometry of numbers of approximation domains, and the Subspace Theorem: parametric, with coefficients in K, with algebraic coefficients, for S-integral points, and in Vojta's general-position form. It then proves the applications — Schmidt's simultaneous approximation, a transcendence criterion, unit equations, decomposable-form, Thue–Mahler, hyperelliptic and norm-form equations, the Corvaja–Zannier gcd bound — and Evertse's quantitative steps: systems of inequalities, the gap principles, the count of small solutions, and the passage from height intervals to subspaces. Twenty-six headline statements are compared: seven forms of Siegel's lemma and Bombieri–Vaaler, seven of Roth's theorem, seven of the Subspace Theorem, and five of Evertse's counting of the subspaces.
entries.title: Heights, Siegel's lemma, Roth's theorem and the Subspace Theorems in Lean

entries.abstract: In the sparse binary-polymer model with reversible ligation and cleavage, fix the food-length bound t, a nonnegative catalysis intensity lambda, and a linear reaction budget Cn. As the maximum polymer length n tends to infinity, the probability of a nonempty reflexively autocatalytic and food-generated reaction set with at most Cn channels tends to zero. The probability that some molecule catalyses a nonempty food-generated reaction set that constructs that molecule also tends to zero. These statements address the linear-size and single-molecule self-construction questions for the sparse catalysis law.
entries.title: Linear-size autocatalytic sets are asymptotically absent in the sparse binary polymer model

entries.abstract: For every integer n >= 1, the standard sequential distributive n-site phosphorylation mechanism admits positive reaction rates and 2n-1 distinct positive stationary states with common positive kinase, phosphatase and substrate totals. The construction establishes a uniform lower bound on the number of positive equilibria of the full mass-action system.
entries.title: Attainment of 2n-1 positive steady states in sequential distributive phosphorylation

entries.abstract: We prove that every source-minimal Type II_l autocatalytic core with l >= 3, reversible mass-action kinetics and strictly positive species degradation has at most one positive stationary state. The result covers the literal weak source grammar, including its separated cyclic realizations and the fully coincident three-species case. Any two positive concentration states satisfying the stationary equations of the same core are equal. The uniqueness theorem is proved in Lean 4 with Mathlib.
entries.title: Unistationarity of Type II_l autocatalytic cores with positive degradation

entries.abstract: Formalization of the irrationality claim for the real value of the Riemann zeta function at five in Aabir Fauzan's September 2026 preprint. The two compared statements assert irrationality of this zeta value and of the sum of reciprocal fifth powers. The development constructs integer polynomials using normalized Hankel determinants, proves positivity and decay estimates, and derives irrationality. The paper's quantitative irrationality-measure claim is not part of this submission.
entries.title: Irrationality of the Riemann zeta value at five

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of p-adic valuations for the restricted binomial gcd G(N;m) = gcd{C(N,k) : 0 < k < N, m divides k}. The principal submitted result gives the complete valuation formula for primes p congruent to -1 modulo m, including the mixed-parity digit-sum branch and the exceptional p = m - 1 valuation-2 case. The repository also proves the complementary p congruent to 1 branch, a prime-power scaling reduction, and complete prime-by-prime formulas for m = 3, 4, and 6.
entries.title: Pascal Minus-One GCD

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of "Homogenization at a polynomial scale in high contrast" by Armstrong, Kuusi and Loher. The paper studies elliptic equations in random media whose conductivity can vary greatly. It proves that their large-scale behavior becomes predictable at a length bounded by a polynomial in the parameters measuring contrast and randomness, improving earlier bounds. The formalization includes quantitative convergence estimates, approximation by an effective constant-coefficient equation, and large-scale regularity results. It builds on the CoarseGraining library.
entries.title: HighContrastHomogenization

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / mathlib formalization of Dana Scott's 1964 paper *Measurement Structures and Linear Inequalities* (Journal of Mathematical Psychology 1 (1964), 233–247). The paper derives necessary and sufficient conditions for three finite representation problems — intransitive indifference, ordered differences, and subjective probability — from the general solvability criterion for finite systems of linear inequalities. The development also covers Scott's ordered-group and signed-charge remarks, literal vector cancellation, and the KPS obstruction to de Finetti's five axioms. Every compared equivalence is described predicate-by-predicate in Challenge.lean and the README, including its numerical-representation side and its qualitative cancellation, permutation, reversal, probability, or Kelley-cover side. The additional infinite theorem is a new, stronger modern characterization first stated in this project; it adapts Kelley's 1959 countable-cover/separation method and is not attributed to Scott. The Lean development was drafted with AI-agent assistance under Lars Warren Ericson's direction and review. Dana S. Scott, Vijay D'Silva, and Brian Milnes are co-authors of the formalization report. There is no sorry outside the deliberate holes in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, and Mathlib is the only Lake dependency.
entries.title: Formalization of Scott's Measurement Structures and Linear Inequalities in Lean 4

entries.abstract: Lean proofs of the ALWZ and Rao–Bell–Chueluecha–Warnke sunflower bounds, robust-sunflower upper and lower bounds, the BCW spread and satisfying results, and the classical Erdős–Rado theorem. The submission compares ten explicit finite statements, including second-moment and Janson routes to the ALWZ bound.
entries.title: Sunflower bounds

entries.abstract: Formalizes two-player bargaining problems with compact convex feasible sets, the four Nash axioms (Pareto optimality, symmetry, invariance to positive affine transformations, independence of irrelevant alternatives), and the Nash product. It proves existence and uniqueness of the Nash product maximizer, shows the maximizer satisfies the four axioms, and proves Nash's characterization: any bargaining solution satisfying the four axioms selects the Nash product maximizer. This is a reusable formalization artifact, not a claim of new mathematics.
entries.title: Nash bargaining solution axiomatic characterization

entries.abstract: Vassena and Stadler conjectured that a reaction network with parameter-rich kinetics cannot have a Hurwitz-unstable Jacobian unless it contains a D-unstable core, a minimal square child-selection submatrix that becomes unstable under positive column scaling. We show that this conjecture is false. We construct a consistent reaction network with four species and five reactions and an admissible reactivity matrix for which the Jacobian has an eigenvalue with strictly positive real part, yet the network has no D-unstable core. Consistency is witnessed by a strictly positive stoichiometric kernel flux, and reactivities are positive exactly on reactant incidences. The counterexample and the resulting negation of the universal necessity statement are proved in Lean 4 with Mathlib.
entries.title: An exact counterexample to the D-unstable-core conjecture for parameter-rich reaction networks

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of the qualitative well-definedness of the nonnegativity Sturm bound A(k) for real level-one modular forms. For every weight k at least 12 and divisible by four, the formalization proves that a finite initial segment detects coefficientwise nonnegativity and that its optimal endpoint is attained as the greatest possible first negative Fourier-coefficient index.
entries.title: Nonnegativity cutoffs for level-one modular forms

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of the corrected nontrivial-tree form of the Csernák--Soukup tree-stacking conjecture. For every finite tree with at least two vertices, the exact-size stacking number equals the explicit rooted-distance-and-degree estimator. The one-vertex case is excluded because the source stacking-number convention restricts admissible thresholds to t >= 2 while the displayed estimator is 1 on the one-vertex tree.
entries.title: Tree stacking equals the Csernák--Soukup estimator on nontrivial finite trees

entries.abstract:
For an infinite set A of positive integers and an integer base b at least 2, consider the reciprocal Mersenne subseries X_A(b) = sum over a in A of 1/(b^a - 1). For a finite nonempty set P of primes, write h_P(a) for the P-part of a. The principal theorem proves irrationality when sum over a in A of h_P(a)/(a*(b^h_P(a) - 1)) converges. The base-two condition implies irrationality at every integer base at least 2 for every infinite subset of the host support. This is a sufficient support criterion, not a solution of the universal Erdős problem. It includes reciprocal-summable supports; the paper credits Erdős for that earlier stated all-base criterion and makes no identification with his suggested weakenings.
The five selected statements also give cofinally arbitrarily small positive weighted displacements, a strengthened positive divisor-cover criterion, and two common-average mixed-support extensions, one using an arbitrary positive weight budget. The proof averages displacements along multiples of a finite divisibility modulus, with another average controlling incomplete periods. Rationality would instead separate every positive displacement from zero. These extensions retain their explicit cover, summability, positivity and infinite-subset assumptions. Full support and all odd exponents are outside the weighted criterion; failure of the criterion is not a rationality assertion. The paper's achievement-set geometry, rational-membership tests and finite-denominator results are outside this registration. This entry supplies independently stated Challenge declarations and matching Lean proofs, with links to the complete paper and reasoning record; it makes no claim of independent human peer review or a novelty verdict.
entries.title: Weighted support criteria for reciprocal Mersenne subseries

entries.abstract: Formalizes finite TU cooperative games, the Shapley value formula, and the four axioms of efficiency, symmetry, the null-player property, and additivity. It proves that the Shapley value satisfies all four and proves uniqueness via unanimity games and Möbius inversion over the Boolean lattice. This is a reusable formalization artifact, not a claim of new mathematics.
entries.title: Shapley value axiomatic characterization

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, built on Mathlib, of the basic theory of locally convex topological vector spaces over the real or complex numbers. It covers barrelled, quasi-barrelled, bornological and ultrabornological spaces; the closed graph and open mapping theorems for barrelled spaces, and Pták's closed graph and open mapping theorems; duality theory with the bipolar, Alaoglu–Bourbaki, Mackey, Mackey–Arens, Banach–Dieudonné and Krein–Šmulian theorems and Grothendieck's completeness theorem; semi-reflexive, reflexive and Montel spaces with their permanence properties; completeness of strong duals; countable strict inductive limits, with the Dieudonné–Schwartz theorem; Milman's converse to the Krein–Milman theorem; and webbed spaces with De Wilde's closed graph and open mapping theorems. The Palomar entry compares 52 theorems from these areas; their statements and the notions they use are in Challenge.lean. The results are classical textbook and research results; the formalization proves them without sorry and without additional axioms.
entries.title: lean-LCS: locally convex spaces, duality, and closed graph theorems in Lean 4

entries.abstract: For every Schatten p-norm with 1 < p < infinity, a finite Hlawka constant exists that does not depend on dimension, and at both endpoints (trace norm, p = 1; operator norm, p = infinity) no constant exists. For complex diagonal matrices and every real p >= 256, the sharp constant is an explicit maximum over a one-parameter cyclic family: it holds in every dimension and cannot be lowered in any dimension at least three.
entries.title: Dimension-independent Hlawka constants for Schatten norms

entries.abstract:
A countable domain R that is a left PCI ring (every cyclic left module not isomorphic to R is injective) and a left V-ring (every simple left module is injective), but is not right Ore, not a right PCI ring and not a right V-ring. Consequently the opposite ring of R is a right PCI ring that is not left PCI.
This answers in the negative the question of Faith (1973), Cozzens and Faith (Simple Noetherian Rings, 1975) and Damiano (1979) whether every right PCI ring is left PCI, and the question, going back to Cozzens and Faith (1975), whether a left V-domain must be a right V-domain.
The ring is an Ore extension K[t; σ, δ] over a free field K (Cohn's universal field of fractions of a free algebra over the rationals) with a non-surjective endomorphism σ, built by iteratively adjoining free solutions of the pseudo-linear equations that govern divisibility of the cyclic modules R/Rf.
The mathematics, the accompanying paper and the Lean code were produced by AI models (Anthropic's Claude) at a human's direction; no human expert has checked the mathematics.
entries.title: A left PCI left V-domain that is not right PCI and not a right V-domain

entries.abstract: Proves that for every topological space X and open cover X = U ∪ V, the inclusion-induced square of Mathlib's ordinary continuous-path fundamental groupoids for U ∩ V, U, V, and X is a pushout in Cat. The statement retains all points as objects and assumes no basepoint, connectedness, or separation conditions. The proof uses continuous paths and endpoint-preserving homotopies, specializes an auxiliary preorder to the indiscrete relation, and proves a natural equivalence with Mathlib's ordinary fundamental groupoid. It constructs the categorical descent functor by path subdivision and proves homotopy invariance by a square subdivision; it does not invoke the imported directed van Kampen theorem.
entries.title: Classical Seifert–van Kampen theorem for the fundamental groupoid

entries.abstract: The least number of edges of a graph of Euclidean dimension five (Erdős–Harary–Tutte) is 15, and both K6 and K1,3,3 attain it (Chaffee and Noble 2016). These are formal-conjectures' erdos_1007.variants.dimension_five and dimension_five_extremal. A graph has dimension n when n is the least dimension in which its vertices can be placed injectively with every edge a unit segment. The lower bound is Chaffee and Noble's Theorem 10: every graph with at most fourteen edges has such a placement in ℝ⁴. Its proof removes a vertex of degree at most three, joins that vertex's neighbours to one another, places the smaller graph by induction, and returns the vertex to one of the infinitely many points at distance one from its neighbours. A graph whose degrees are all at least four has at most seven vertices, and those graphs are handled case by case. For attainment, K6 has dimension five because six points at pairwise distance one fit in ℝ⁵ but not in ℝ⁴. K1,3,3 has dimension five by Theorem 8: it has an explicit placement in ℝ⁵, and an orthogonal-complement count rules out ℝ⁴. The supporting results are in GraphDimension, a separate Lean library on the dimension of graphs, which this repository pins by revision. The question belongs to discrete geometry and extremal graph theory, specifically the study of unit-distance representations and the dimension of graphs.
entries.title: Erdős 1007, dimension five: fifteen edges, attained by K6 and K1,3,3

entries.abstract: For the four-corner Cantor set approximants K_n = C_n × C_n, where C_n is the union of the 2^n intervals of length 4^{-n} with left endpoints sum_{j<=n} w_j 4^{-j}, w_j in {0,3}, let α_Fav be the supremum of the a >= 0 for which the Favard length Fav(K_n) = (1/π) ∫_0^π |π_θ(K_n)| dθ is at most C n^{-a} for all n >= 1. This project proves in Lean that every a < 1/4 is admissible, so 1/4 <= α_Fav, together with the classical bound α_Fav <= 1. The previous best lower bounds were 1/6 (Nazarov-Peres-Volberg, 2010) and 1/5 (Marshall, arXiv:2509.02882 v2, 2026, whose v1 claim of 1/4 was withdrawn). The new ingredient is a joint negative-moment estimate for the low-frequency cosine product. The argument comes from an unpublished AI-assisted manuscript, and this formalization is its first complete proof.
entries.title: The Favard-length decay exponent of the four-corner Cantor set is at least 1/4

entries.abstract: Source-based formalization of the classical Stallings finite-graph recognition theorem. It gives an executable finite folding construction for every finite list of words in the rank-two free group, with exact subgroup-membership correctness. The least deterministic fold congruence is computed by finite exhaustive search; there is no complexity claim or implementation of core trimming, subgroup bases, intersections, or index algorithms.
entries.title: Verified finite automata for finitely generated subgroups of F₂

entries.abstract: A graph has dimension n when n is the least number such that its vertices can be placed injectively in ℝⁿ with every edge of length one (Erdős, Harary and Tutte). House proved that a graph of dimension four has at least nine edges, and that nine is attained only by K_{3,3}. This project proves the second half in Lean 4, in the form google-deepmind/formal-conjectures states it as erdos_1007.variants.dimension_four_extremal: a graph of dimension four with nine edges and no isolated vertex is isomorphic to K_{3,3}. The proof follows Chaffee and Noble's proof of House's theorem. On the way it proves that K_{3,3} has dimension exactly four and that every graph with at most eight edges has a unit-distance representation in ℝ³ (Chaffee–Noble, Theorem 6).
entries.title: Unit-distance graphs of dimension four with nine edges

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of eighteen selected Phase 1 statements, led by a single positive lower natural-density constant for the set of positive integers reaching 1 within c log x ordinary Collatz steps, valid for every fixed c > 3/log(4/3). It also covers fixed-target hitting, the exact target criterion, individual-root consequences, vanishing-clock-loss variants, depth-eleven density bounds, exact finite fan allocation, real-moment comparison, target profiles, and bounded actual reference entropy with explicit tail estimates and zero normalized growth. Density witnesses and levels are existential. Full optimized formulas, complementary capacity, the Renyi-order right limit, amplified roots, and convergence of every positive integer remain outside the formalized scope.
entries.title: Positive density of Collatz convergence at every rate above 3/log(4/3)

entries.abstract:
Explicit zero-density results for the Riemann zeta function in short intervals, formalized in Lean 4 over Mathlib.  Count the nontrivial zeros whose imaginary part lies in a window (t-h, t+h], with multiplicity and with a zero on either horizontal edge counted for half.
Seven statements are submitted, and all seven are mechanically checked.  Two are zero-density bounds for the edge strip Re s > 1-alpha, valid for 0 <= h <= t^(2/3), proved by two different mechanisms -- Jensen's formula and Littlewood's lemma, the source's Theorems 2 and 3.  Neither dominates the other over the whole parameter range.  Two turn those into bounds on the fraction of the window's zeros lying in that strip, and are antitone in both h0 and t0, so one evaluation bounds every larger window: Corollaries 4 and 5.  The remaining three are the headline corollary, Corollary 1 -- for every alpha in (0, 1/6) there are h0 and t0 beyond which a definite fraction of the window's zeros, bounded below by an explicit POSITIVE constant, have real part in the middle band [alpha, 1-alpha], away from both edges of the critical strip.  One states it with the constant named, one with the constant existentially quantified as the source phrases it, and one at the explicit parameters alpha = 1/16 with a sharper radius, where the limiting constant is 9/25.
The positivity is proved, not assumed, and needs no numerics: every term of the constant except the leading one carries a factor 1/h or 1/log t, so it tends to a limit fixed by one rational inequality, which the radius 1/2 discharges for every admissible alpha.  The factor of two relating the two edge strips is the reflection rho -> 1 - conj(rho), proved in the development to be a multiplicity-preserving involution of the zero set.
The results are conditional and their hypotheses are in the signature, not hidden.  They are of two kinds, kept apart in the development because a reader is entitled to weigh them differently.  Sixteen are published explicit bounds on zeta and Gamma transcribed from other authors; eleven are finite numerical certificates established outside Lean by arb ball arithmetic or mpmath on explicit compact boxes, which Mathlib cannot currently reproduce because it has no verified evaluation of zeta and the margins reach 9e-17.  The source's tables give the numerical values of the constant; they are not load-bearing for its sign.
`comparator.json` names exactly those seven and is the authority on what is checked.  Beyond them, the wider development supplies what they rest on: the Littlewood short-interval theorem (Theorem 32), the argument-integral machinery (Theorem 31), the appendix of explicit zeta bounds, the Laurent expansion of zeta'/zeta, and the reflection step.
entries.title: Zero density theorems for short intervals

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg partial regularity theory for suitable weak solutions of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with forcing in L^q, q > 5/2: the L^3 epsilon-regularity theorem (Theorem A), the gradient epsilon-regularity criterion (Theorem B) and the vanishing of the one-dimensional parabolic Hausdorff measure of the singular set (Theorem C). The three theorems are proved using only the standard axioms, restated together in a Mathlib-only comparator challenge and proved from the library theorems. The manuscript being formalized is in the repository and was corrected alongside the development.
entries.title: CaffarelliKohnNirenberg

entries.abstract: Lean 4 proofs of the algebraic results in Small undecidable groups and unrecognizable 4-manifolds (arXiv:2609.10461v1): existence of a group with a three-generator, nine-relator presentation and unsolvable word problem; an effective family of four-generator, eleven-relator presentations with undecidable triviality; and an effective family of two-generator, ten-relator presentations with undecidable triviality. These are Theorems 1.1, 1.3, and 1.4 of the paper. The four-manifold consequences in the paper are outside the formalized scope.
entries.title: Small undecidable groups and fixed-size Adian–Rabin families

entries.abstract: For every c > 4, an explicit polynomial ODE on Euclidean five-space has a compact global attractor and uniformly negative divergence. Its finite-time local Lyapunov dimension at every positive real time and its asymptotic Kaplan--Yorke dimension have maximum 4 + 4/c, attained precisely on an invariant two-torus with irrational angular flow. The maximum over equilibria and periodic points is 3. All singular-value exponents exist, and local dimensions converge pointwise. This disproves the unrestricted form of Eden's conjecture; the attractor is not assumed transitive.
entries.title: A counterexample to the unrestricted form of Eden's conjecture

entries.abstract: SCOPE and REACH are integrable unbiased estimators of an outcome-before-stopping probability for autoregressive models on countably infinite vocabularies. REACH is the conditional expectation of a two-stage Monte Carlo estimator given the outcome-free backbones. Its variance bound against ordinary Monte Carlo is derived from that Rao–Blackwell identity and the law of total variance, for every positive sample count. The development also proves the stopping-time property, almost-sure finiteness, and the bridge between the two sampling experiments.
entries.title: SCOPE and REACH with almost-surely finite stopping times

entries.abstract: The real field expanded by the function $x\mapsto A(1+x^2)$, where $A$ is a normalized analytic Abel function for $e^x-1$, is an o-minimal structure that defines a function that grows faster than any finite iterate of the exponential function.
entries.title: A transexponential o-minimal structure

entries.abstract: Formalizes the exact minimum AND-gate counts 0, 1, 3, 6 and 9 for binary polynomial multiplication with zero through four coefficients per operand. XOR and constants are free, and AND inputs may reuse arbitrary earlier nonlinear wires. The principal result excludes eight-gate four-term circuits and matches an explicit nine-gate construction. Separate research workflows check selected n5 quadratic results and n6 upper bounds and reductions; their open unrestricted/bilinear lower bounds are not claims of this submission.
entries.title: Unrestricted Boolean multiplicative complexity of four-term polynomial multiplication

entries.abstract: Let D_k(N) be the largest size of a subset of {1, ..., N} with no positive k-th-power difference. We prove D_k(N) >= c_k N^alpha_k for every N >= 1, with positive constants c_k and exponents 0.75806770413, 0.9142, and 0.95295 for squares, fourth powers, and sixth powers. The proofs use a general interval-moment criterion for every positive integer k. We also prove arithmetic lifting results, exact product and prime-depth laws for interval capacity, and existence of the binary square capacity limit. The square construction refines Naslund's published example while retaining its binary transition rules. All selected statements are proved in Lean.
entries.title: Lower bounds for sets without perfect-power differences

entries.abstract: Arithmetic regular configurations with private prime pivots, exact source–target Palm mass identities, ordinary deletion and normalized deficit bounds. The independent target is regular with probability tending to one, while absolute cumulant activity has a positive normalized lower bound on prime scales for original and stronger retained sets.
entries.title: Regular configurations, Palm deficits and the cumulant obstruction

entries.abstract: Quantitative comparison of the actual position/excess/sign field at growing intensity, retaining the original small-prime conditioning; same-grid dyadic restriction and common measurable readouts. Along literal dyadic scales, empirical window counts converge almost surely to Poisson, while empirical full vectors have a positive total-variation obstruction.
entries.title: Microscopic signed fields and empirical Poisson laws

entries.abstract: This project formalizes all five main results of arXiv:2502.09871, "An atomic decomposition of one-dimensional metric currents without boundary" (Chen, Goodman, Hernandez, Spector), in Lean 4 against Mathlib.
entries.title: An atomic decomposition of one-dimensional metric currents without boundary

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of manuscript Theorem 2.4: for every finite field K with |K| at least 4 and every m at least 1, a coordinatewise-affine strategy on the class of size |K|-1 cannot be completed to a winning strategy by arbitrary deterministic rules on the opposite class of size m, with respect to the fixed finite-field labeling.
entries.title: One-Sided Affine Obstructions in Complete Bipartite Hat Guessing

entries.abstract: Conditioned on the presence of a run contained in a finite prefix, the first such run has a mixture law combining a microscopic border contribution with a uniform bulk location, geometric excess and fair sign. The results retain the marked record, describe both location scales in finite and infinite phase regimes, and determine the sign bias. Under compatible affine conditions on small primes, the border probability is exactly 2^(-d), where d is the row-space deficit. Affine localization and sign bias use the rank information budget without future neutrality; the full marked-clock limit also requires eventual neutrality for each fixed finite future prefix. Approximation uses the prime number theorem, the Poisson process estimate of Arratia, Goldstein and Gordon, and the stated Laishram–Shorey, Shorey and Nicolas–Robin estimates. The exact affine border identity needs none of these literature hypotheses.
entries.title: Microscopic–bulk crossover and conditional affine laws

entries.abstract: The exact left-border probability is 2^(-pi(L)), and the microscopic non-vacancy probability satisfies 0 <= q_L/2^(-pi(L)) - 1 <= 2^(-pi(L)/256) for sufficiently large L. The results give conditional localization and uniqueness, stability under changes of mesoscopic cutoff, and a quantitative Poisson law for runs contained in a finite prefix. They yield the critical longest-run distribution and asymmetric almost-sure envelopes for all integer prefix lengths. The exact border identity needs no literature hypothesis. The asymptotic results use, as applicable, scalar Stein bounds, the prime number theorem, the uniform prime-divisor estimate of Laishram and Shorey, Shorey's square-product exclusion, and the divisor bound of Nicolas and Robin.
entries.title: Microscopic boundary, prefixes and longest runs

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of the finite-poset theorem that any finite poset with at most fifteen elements, width at most three, and the CI2 common-incomparability condition has at most forty-eight antichains.
entries.title: The order-six stable-marriage finite-poset bound

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of Mikko Fischer's explicit connected 24-vertex subcubic graph with independence number 9 and zero-forcing number 11. The formalization verifies the exact graph and both numerical invariants, yielding an existential counterexample to the proposed bound Z(G) <= alpha(G) + 1 for connected graphs of maximum degree at most 3.
entries.title: Fischer's 24-vertex zero-forcing counterexample

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 proof of the negative answer to Erdős problem 973: power sums of complex numbers on or outside the unit circle cannot all be exponentially small. For each fixed C > 1 and all sufficiently large n, any n such numbers have some order 2 ≤ k ≤ n+1 with |∑_i z_i^k| > C^(-n), even without the original condition z₁ = 1. The proof follows the residual-polynomial method in Tan, Wang, Huang, and Chen’s August 2026 paper “Residual bounds for Schur-stable polynomials,” using a fixed-degree polynomial test. This submission provides a complete machine-checked proof of the negative answer previously obtained by Luo, Yang, and Zhu.
entries.title: Erdős 973: power sums cannot all be exponentially small

entries.abstract: Joint Poisson–Gaussian limits for conditioned run counts, with an autoregressive Gaussian target and independent normal innovations. Quantitative results give local Poisson probabilities, a Gaussian distribution-function bound, moderate deviations, and relative local or tail estimates for the multiplicative source under the stated information budgets. The whole integer-level point process has locally finite but infinite total mass; its complete upper-half laws, conditioning on a fixed count and extreme phases are included. The two upper-half law assertions include proved measurability and probability normalization; conditioning on every finite count has positive mass. The intrinsic probability estimates are proved internally. Their arithmetic applications use, as applicable, the prime number theorem, scalar Stein bounds, the Poisson process estimate of Arratia, Goldstein and Gordon, and Barbour's corrected multivariate Stein bounds.
entries.title: Threshold staircases and the Poisson–Gaussian bridge

entries.abstract:
Besicovitch's 1/2-conjecture asserts that a Borel set in the plane with finite one-dimensional Hausdorff measure whose lower density exceeds 1/2 almost everywhere is countably 1-rectifiable. Writing sigma_1(R^2) for the least threshold that forces countable 1-rectifiability, the conjecture is sigma_1(R^2) = 1/2. The previously published record is sigma_1(R^2) <= 7/10, obtained by De Lellis, Glaudo, Massaccesi and Vittone.
This development proves, with a complete Lean 4 proof term, sigma_1(H) <= 6934/10000 = 0.6934 for every real Hilbert space H, without finite-dimensionality or separability assumptions.
entries.title: A machine-checked bound of 0.6934 for Besicovitch's 1/2-problem

entries.abstract: For deterministic stationary root-finding methods without memory, the Kung–Traub bound 2^(n-1) for n >= 1 real or complex scalar derivative observations, the bound given by the first group size times the product of one plus each subsequent size for prescribed positive groups, and entire counterexamples, including one real witness defeating every larger real exponent simultaneously. A concrete inverse Hermite method attains 2^(n-1) for n >= 2 on open real intervals and has that exact order on exp(x)-1. Supporting constructions are included.
entries.title: A formal proof of the Kung–Traub conjecture

entries.abstract: Complete Lean proof of the revised SparseStack main theorem through its retained-count route. For every fixed real isometry, the actual independent uniform signed-bucket sketch with the rounded C=80, B=169/20 prescription has Gram-norm failure probability at most delta. The same prescription satisfies s<26.35 q/eps and m<176.9(d+q)/eps^2. All physical channel estimates and the all-order scalar certificate are proved.
entries.title: Improved SparseStack Constants

entries.abstract: Poisson comparisons for word dictionaries, including mean distances for uniformly sampled fixed-size and affine dictionaries with each dictionary held fixed inside the comparison. Exact excesses and signs, category aggregation, geometric marks and compound Poisson cluster laws are retained.
entries.title: Typical dictionaries, exact marks and compound Poisson clusters

entries.abstract: Poisson laws for the actual run field with positions, all excesses and signs; hard and soft small-prime conditioning, deterministic masks and statistics, stable recorded variables, uniform quenched convergence, and an information-adapted cutoff that respects a prescribed conditioning floor.
entries.title: Critical Poisson fields and information-adapted conditioning

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 proof of Erdős problem 689: for all sufficiently large n, one residue class per prime p ≤ n can cover every integer from 1 through n at least twice. The proof follows the argument for Theorem 1.1 in Chojecki’s April 2026 manuscript “A greedy matching proof of Erdős’s two-fold residue-class problem.” The formalization directly proves the required three-prime counting estimate using Fourier analysis, replacing the manuscript’s invocation of Green–Tao, and verifies the sieve bounds and greedy-matching construction in Lean.
entries.title: Erdős 689: eventual double covering by prime residue classes

entries.abstract: A Mathlib-only nonempty finite-simplex, algorithmic specialization of Theorem 4 in Dann, Mansour, Mohri, Schneider, and Sivan (COLT 2025). It realizes the tensor action space as a joint simplex, defines the source improper comparator by adding a mixed-constraint tensor of the canonical action marginal, proves that comparator escapes the action set, and proves exact finite-horizon equality between approachability loss and improper phi-regret under explicit causal strategy translations in both directions. It also proves that every joint action is a mixture of at most one rank-one tensor per constraint index.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Finite tight Blackwell approachability-to-improper phi-regret reduction in Lean

entries.abstract: We prove a general interval-moment criterion for square-difference-free integer sets and apply it to obtain an improved unconditional lower bound in Sarkozy's theorem, with exponent 0.75806746. If D(N) is the largest size of a subset of {1, ..., N} containing no two distinct elements whose difference is a square, then for every epsilon > 0 and all sufficiently large N we prove D(N) >= N^(0.75806746 - epsilon). The exact exponent is 37903373/50000000. The reusable criterion starts from finite digit sets in pairwise coprime square bases, with ordered intervals and width-moment inequalities. A strict surplus in the component exponents yields the asymptotic bound through finite stopping words, rank rounding, the Chinese remainder theorem, and interpolation between geometric scales. Both the general criterion and its numerical application are formalized in Lean. All nine concrete components are proved: six prime chains, a 25-state binary recursion, and the two complete composite witnesses for 215 and 437. Every required ordering, numerical moment, lifting, and asymptotic argument is checked, with no remaining finite-certificate hypotheses. The repository includes self-contained PDF and LaTeX write-ups of the full result and a simpler companion construction attaining exponent 0.758001 that explains several core ideas, together with exact computational certificate programs. The simpler construction is not separately formalized or a selected submission statement.
entries.title: An interval-moment criterion for square-difference-free integer sets

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the relative consistency of ZFC + CH together with the following assertion. There is a countably saturated elementary extension of the natural-number arithmetic structure of cardinality aleph one; all such set-sized presentations are isomorphic; and no such presentation is ordinal definable. The class is defined without parameters. Removing CH from the asserted theory gives a consistent negative answer to MathOverflow question 382009 about definability up to isomorphism versus an ordinal-definable copy. Every notion in the final sentence is internal to the first-order model of set theory.
entries.title: definable-saturated

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib proof that the 7-adic zeta value ζ₇(3) is irrational. Here ζ₇(3) = L₇(3, ω⁻²) is the Kubota–Leopoldt value, equal to the 7-adic limit of the Euler-corrected Bernoulli numbers −(1 − 7^{w−1}) B_w / w over the weights w = 6·7^{n+1} − 2. The same is proved for η = ζ₇(3)/2. The proof is a determinant irrationality argument on the modular curve X₀(7), in four parts: independence of seven explicit germs attached to the weight −2 seven-adic Eisenstein series, with a uniform zero estimate; a seven-adic annular saving; an auxiliary-prime denominator estimate; and an Archimedean energy estimate with a kernel-checked numerical margin. It also uses an internal proof of the geometric continuation of the target series to every radius below 49, via a twisted U₇ matrix bound and initial overconvergence obtained from classical Eisenstein approximants. The Lean endpoints depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The mathematical argument has not been refereed. The work is human-directed, with extensive AI assistance in both the mathematics and the Lean development; see the automation section and PROVENANCE.md.
entries.title: Irrationality of the 7-adic zeta value ζ₇(3)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Brydges-Kennedy-Abdesselam-Rivasseau forest interpolation formula: for a finite vertex set V and a C-infinity function rho on the edge-coupling space of the complete graph on V, the value of rho at the all-ones coupling equals the sum, over all acyclic edge subsets (forests) F, of the integral over the unit cube [0,1]^E(F) of the mixed partial derivative of rho in the edge variables of F, evaluated at the path-minimum interpolation point x^F(u); the empty forest contributes rho(0). The flagship theorem is additionally restated Mathlib-only and re-proved in the leanprover/comparator challenge/solution format using Audit/ForestFormula/comparator.json.
entries.title: BKARForestFormula

entries.abstract:
Lean proofs of Hausdorff dimension at least n-(n-k)/p_c^k for all (n,k)-Besicovitch sets with 1<=k<=n, and positive Lebesgue measure for Lebesgue measurable such sets when p_c^(k-1)+k>n. Here a Besicovitch set contains a translated unit k-disk in every k-dimensional direction, and p_c is the unique root in (2,3) of p^3-2p^2-2p+2=0.
Building on Bourgain's arithmetic-combinatorial approach, Nets Hawk Katz and Terence Tao's New bounds for Kakeya problems (2002; preprint 2001) established the Minkowski-dimension bound 1+(n-1)/beta_c, where beta_c=p_c/(p_c-1)=1.67513... satisfies beta_c^3-4*beta_c+2=0. This is exactly n-(n-1)/p_c, so the numerical exponent itself is not new. They also proved the distinct Hausdorff bound (2-sqrt(2))*(n-4)+3. A Minkowski lower bound alone does not imply the same Hausdorff lower bound: Hausdorff dimension is at most Minkowski dimension.
Richard Oberlin's subsequent X-ray work (2006 preprint; published 2010) gave the Hausdorff bound n-(n-k)/(1+sqrt(2))^k and positive measure when (1+sqrt(2))^(k-1)+k>n. Later polynomial-partitioning work by Hickman, Rogers, and Zhang improved Kakeya bounds in many dimensions while retaining the large-dimension leading coefficient 2-sqrt(2).
The claimed advance here is a continuous projection estimate with joint measurable parameter selection, developed from the supplied September 2026 manuscript. Its mixed-norm X-ray and plate maximal consequences, together with a countable-cover argument, give the Katz-Tao numerical bound for Hausdorff dimension and replace 1+sqrt(2)=2.41421... by p_c=2.48119... in Oberlin's displayed dimension and positive-measure ranges. For k=1 the resulting Hausdorff bound is approximately 0.596968*n+0.403032, with a larger leading coefficient than 2-sqrt(2)=0.585786.... This is an improvement in sufficiently high dimensions, not a claim to the best bound in every dimension. The formalized hypotheses require only unit disks, and the Hausdorff theorem requires neither measurability nor boundedness of the set.
Both geometric theorems and the exact bounds 2.481<p_c<2.482 are proved with only the standard Lean axioms. The comparisons above identify the improvement over the cited results; independent mathematical review and confirmation of novelty against the full literature remain pending. Final sandboxed Comparator and independent-kernel verification are pending.
entries.title: NKBesicovitch

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of a geometric strengthening/variant of Pablo Soberón's counterexample to the Grünbaum four-hyperplane mass-partition conjecture.
