The formalized result constructs a convex body K in R^4 with nonempty interior such that no four affine hyperplanes divide K into sixteen sign cells of equal four-dimensional volume.  Equivalently, the obstructed mass can be chosen to be uniform Lebesgue volume on a convex body.  The proof adapts Soberón's explicit cubic/quartic tensor obstruction and replaces the smooth positive density used in the source by a small Wulff-body perturbation of the Euclidean ball.
entries.title: A convex body variant of Soberon's counterexample to the Grünbaum conjecture.

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, on top of Mathlib, of the classical function theory of several complex variables on open subsets of finite-dimensional complex normed spaces, with values in complex Banach spaces wherever the statements allow. The compared statements cover: Cauchy's integral formula on polydiscs, Osgood's lemma, the equivalence of holomorphy and analyticity, the Cauchy-Riemann equations, Cauchy estimates, the identity theorem, the maximum modulus principle, holomorphic dependence of integrals and the Cauchy-Pompeiu identity; the theorems of Weierstrass, Montel and Vitali and an estimate for holomorphic L^p classes; the holomorphic inverse and implicit mapping theorems; Reinhardt domains, logarithmic convexity, the characterization of convergence domains of power series, Laurent expansion, and continuation from Reinhardt and circular domains; Hartogs-Taylor expansion, Hartogs' continuity theorem, Hartogs' theorem on separate analyticity, removability of isolated singularities, the two Riemann extension theorems and Hartogs' extension theorem for compact holes; elementary analytic sets and their regular points; the local ring of analytic germs, Weierstrass division and preparation, and the Noetherian and unique factorization properties of the germ ring; injective holomorphic maps, Cartan's uniqueness theorem, linearity of biholomorphisms of circular domains, transitivity of the automorphisms of the ball and the inequivalence of ball and polydisc; holomorphic hulls, domains of holomorphy, Thullen's lemma, the Cartan-Thullen theorem and Bochner's tube theorem; subharmonic and plurisubharmonic functions, the Levi form, pseudoconvexity of domains of holomorphy, Levi's theorem and local peak functions; Runge domains and polynomial hulls. All results are classical; none is claimed to be new.
entries.title: Several complex variables: local theory, Hartogs phenomena, Weierstrass theory, domains of holomorphy and pseudoconvexity

entries.abstract: Let C be an infinite real plane algebraic curve defined by a polynomial of degree d >= 2 that is irreducible over the complex numbers, and suppose C is not a circle. Its group of Euclidean symmetries is finite, the orientation-preserving part is cyclic of order at most max(d, 2d - 4), and the full group has order at most 2d. Both bounds are attained in every degree d >= 2. For d >= 5, curves attaining the rotation bound are exactly, up to orientation-preserving similarity, the curves Re(z^(d-2)(|z|^2 + a)) = 0 with |a| = 1 and a not real; conversely each such curve with d - 2 >= 3 attains the bound. This entry formalizes Theorem 1 of the note; the note's second theorem (Mobius symmetries and genus of the extremal family) is not part of this entry.
entries.title: Sharp symmetry bounds for real plane algebraic curves (Theorem 1)

entries.abstract: We reformulate Birnbaum's theorem as a statement about classes of statistical procedures that preserve statistical relations, and show that the proof reduces to the propagation of evidential equality along chains of conditionality-related inference bases (experiment–observation pairs). For finite parameter spaces with at least two points, the sufficiency relation and the conditionality relation are incomparable, yet the corresponding preservation classes are nested. The class of likelihood-invariant procedures with codomain [0, 1] is strictly contained in the class of sufficiency-invariant procedures. The lower-tail likelihood-ratio p-value illustrates this strict inclusion.
entries.title: Birnbaum’s principles in Venn diagrams: Extended version with Lean verification

entries.abstract:
A machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the principal population-gap perturbation results of Yi Yu, Tengyao Wang and Richard J. Samworth, "A useful variant of the Davis-Kahan theorem for statisticians" (Biometrika 102 (2015) 315-323). This single Palomar entry compares both conclusions of Theorem 2 and both displays of Corollary 1 for eigenspaces of real symmetric matrices, together with the right- and left-singular-subspace conclusions of Theorem 3 for general real matrices and two supporting equivalences between its Gram-eigenvector formulation and the paper's paired singular-vector equations.
The common idea is that every separation hypothesis in Theorems 2 and 3 is stated entirely in terms of the population object. Theorem 2 uses the population eigenvalue gap min(lambda_(r-1)-lambda_r, lambda_s-lambda_(s+1)); Theorem 3 applies the same idea to the squared singular spectrum, with the additional factor (2 sigma_1 + ||A-hat-A||_op). No sample eigenvalue or singular-value gap is assumed, so the sample frame is arbitrary among admissible orthonormal frames at the selected block, including under multiplicity.
The selected results have deliberately different source dispositions. Theorem 2 is source-exact. Corollary 1 writes out the unit normalization inherited from its introduction as the d=1 case of Theorem 2; the standalone printed display omits that normalization and its second conclusion is false without it. Theorem 3 is source-corrected: its printed convention sigma^2_(rank(A)+1) := -infinity makes the denominator infinite at a rank boundary and yields a false assertion. The compared statement instead uses the ambient Gram-spectrum convention used by the paper's own proof, with singular values zero past rank, while retaining the printed restriction 1 <= r <= s <= rank(A). Because this one entry contains that correction, its source relationship is conservatively recorded as `adapts`.
entries.title: Yu-Wang-Samworth 2015: population-gap eigenspace and singular-subspace perturbation bounds

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 classification of the number of good partitions of an initial interval, where a good partition of {1, ..., n} is a set of pairwise disjoint nonempty blocks of at most three integers covering {1, ..., n}, each block summing to a power of three, and count n is the number of them. With N_u = {1, 2, 3, 4} union {3^t - 4, 3^t - 2, 3^t - 1, 3^t, 3^t + 1, 3^t + 2, 3^t + 3, 3^t + 5 : t >= 2} and E_2 = {13} union {3^t - 3 : t >= 2} union {3^t - 6 : t >= 3}, the four compared theorems say that for n >= 1 the count is 1 exactly on N_u, is 2 exactly on E_2, and is at least 3 elsewhere, and that the count is 2 at every 3^t - 6 with t >= 3. The source proves uniqueness for every n in N_u, records exactly two partitions at 3^t - 3 and at 13, and conjectures, immediately after that theorem, more than two at every other n, reporting a computer check up to n = 844; the family 3^t - 6 (first member 21) refutes that conjecture as printed, and the converse of the uniqueness statement is proved here. The lower bounds are three explicit partitions transported by four constructions each of which keeps a recoverable component; the exact values are exhaustive enumerations at twenty values n <= 86, kernel-checked and complete by a theorem about the search, carried to every power of three by stabilization above a threshold.
entries.title: gnm-lean: the number of partitions of {1, ..., n} into sets of at most three elements with power-of-three sums

entries.abstract: Lean4 formalization of the Komlós bound with constant 36 following the Lovett—Karingula exposition. The Komlós statement gives signs for finitely many vectors of Euclidean norm at most 1 so that the signed sum has supremum norm at most 36. The Beck–Fiala statement gives a vertex colouring with edge discrepancy at most 36√t when every vertex belongs to at most t edges.
entries.title: Komlós conjecture

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of four principal endpoint assertions from Fragkos, Krause, and Lacey's Endpoint Estimates for Stein's Purely Quadratic Carleson Operator: two failures of modular estimates below t log₂ t, a full-modulation L log L endpoint estimate, and a lacunary L (log₂ L)² log₄ L endpoint estimate.
entries.title: Endpoint estimates for Stein's purely quadratic Carleson operator

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of the quantitative theory of advection-diffusion in self-similar random incompressible flows: the superdiffusive asymptotics of the effective diffusivity (Theorem A), the renormalization of the generator (quantitative homogenization of the Dirichlet problem at every scale, Theorem B), and the anomalous large-scale regularity theory (Theorem C) of Armstrong-Bou-Rabee-Kuusi, together with the sensitivity and coarse-matrix-derivative theory, the diffusivity recursion, and the diffusion-process theory that support them. The formalization consumes the public CoarseGraining homogenization library as its analytic base and the public MarkovProcess library for the general theory of continuous strong Markov processes of Feller semigroups. The three headline theorems are independently checked using the SuperdiffusionAudit/ comparator pairs.
entries.title: Superdiffusion

entries.abstract:
A Lean 4 formalization of the theorem FriedCrossing.fried_counterexample_of_resolvent_inputs, the machine-checked reduction behind a proposed codimension-one failure of Fried's identity ζ(0) = τ_R for acyclic characters on a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold with b₁ = 1. For a simple illustration of the method with figures, see docs/counterexample_intuitive_view.pdf.
The Mechanism: Near (g_hyp, ρ_triv), along the conformal family g_τ = e^{−2τb}g_hyp with characters χ_θ, the Ruelle resonances near 0 form two small clusters: a rank-2 cluster in degree 1, encoded by a 2×2 matrix M(θ,τ), and a rank-4 cluster in degree 2, encoded by a 4×4 matrix A(θ,τ). A branch is one eigenvalue of a cluster matrix followed continuously in (θ,τ). Degree 1 has the closed branch and the twin s_nc(θ,τ), which starts at the double point s*(θ) < 0 and travels at rate r₀ > 0 towards 0. Degree 2 has the two locked branches (the same eigenvalues, lifted by d₀) and two pure branches, the roots of Q = X² − e₁X + e₂; the pure branch nearest 0 is z(θ,τ). At the crossing metric τ = σ(θ) the twin and z reach 0 together, the twin as a pole of ζ and z as a zero, so ζ stays regular at 0 and ζ(0; g_σ) = τ_R · (rate of the twin)/(rate of z). The twin's rate is at most 2r₀ and z's exceeds 2r₀, so ζ(0; g_σ) ≠ τ_R. Fried's identity would need the two branches to arrive at the same speed. The whole Lean argument is bookkeeping of these four branches.
What is Proved: The theorem is a conditional reduction. Its objects are two abstract resolvent families on Banach scales (structure fields = the cited facts: local uniform boundedness and two-sided inversion of the generator modulo inclusions, CDDP Lemma 4.3; smooth generator), complex structures, and nondegenerate frames; the cluster matrices M, A are DEFINED from them as real parts of the frame matrices A(p)⁻¹B(p) built from contour integrals of matrix elements of the resolvent. Its hypotheses are, in six groups, the properties of that data which the argument uses, each cited: (1) two independent states at s*(θ) in the degree-1 cluster at τ = 0, with s*(0) = 0, s* continuous, s*(θ) < 0 for θ ≠ 0 [DGRS (7.6), BuOl Cor 5.1, DFG Thm 2; independence = rederivation A2 of the informal account]; (2) the first-variation formula B·∂_τM(0,0) = diag(0,p) with r₀ = B_cc p/det B > 0 [CDDP (4.22), (1.3)]; (3) the degree-2 cluster at τ = 0 has spectrum {s*, s*, s*, −s*} [DGRS (7.6), k = 2]; (4) at θ = 0 the degree-1 cluster is singular and the degree-2 cluster has spectrum {0, 0, 0, tr M} [CDDP Cor 4.1, DGRS Lemma 7.1]; (5) every eigenvalue of M is an eigenvalue of A [DGRS Lemma 7.1]; (6) for any functions ζ₀, F, any τ_R ≠ 0 and dimension vector c: ζ₀ = F·z/s_nc off the crossing with F continuous and ζ₀(σ) = F(σ) at it [CD (6.5) at λ = 0], ζ₀ = τ_R wherever s_nc ≠ 0 [DGRS Thm 2 + Fried 1986], exactness of C₀¹ → C₀² → V₃ at each crossing [DR Thm 2.1], c₀ = c₄ = 0 and c₃ = c₁ [DGRS Lemmas 7.4, 7.2], c_k the dimensions. The conclusion: there are θ₀, δ > 0 such that for 0 < |θ| < θ₀ the twin crosses 0 at exactly one σ ∈ (0, 2|s*|/r₀], the ζ-order at 0 is zero, the zero branch has slope ∂_τe₂/e₁ of modulus > 2r₀, |e₁(θ,σ)| ≤ K₁|θ|σ, and ζ₀(σ) = τ_R · (pole rate)/(zero rate) ≠ τ_R, with the torsion identity of the zero cluster.
Dependencies: The identification of the abstract data with the geometry — that the resolvent families are those of the twisted deformed generator L_X + iθω(X) on the anisotropic spaces of g_τ, that ζ₀(τ) is the Ruelle zeta function of g_τ at 0, that τ_R is the Reidemeister torsion of χ_θ, and that the defined matrices are the cluster matrices (their imaginary parts vanish) — is the informal layer, taken from the cited papers and the accompanying note, and is not formalized. Nothing about manifolds, flows, anisotropic spaces or zeta functions is in Lean. Granting the six groups as cited, the theorem exhibits a counterexample to Fried's identity in the form stated by DGRS for acyclic unitary representations, at a non-generic metric where ζ is regular at 0 and zero-resonant states exist with cancelling multiplicities; the refined identity of CD Thm 4 holds there. Whether the six groups hold as cited has not been independently verified by a mathematician other than the author.
entries.title: Resonance-cluster analysis for a proposed counterexample to Fried's conjecture

entries.abstract: Formalizes the exact centered-xi coefficient normalization, a uniform sectorial saddle-point asymptotic, and relative-error derivative estimates through order six. These are the analytic inputs used by a two-thirds hyperbolicity-wedge theorem for Jensen polynomials of Riemann's xi-function. This Palomar topic does not itself state the final Jensen-polynomial hyperbolicity theorem.
entries.title: Sectorial asymptotics for centered Riemann-xi coefficients

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 + mathlib formalization of Fan Chang, Hong Liu, and Miao Liu's paper "A proof of Chvátal's conjecture via a sharp correlation inequality" (arXiv:2609.19123v1). It formalizes their star theorem for hereditary set families, sharp Boolean Fourier correlation inequality, antipodal corollary, sharpness results, and weighted strengthening. The formalization was completely prepared by GPT-6.
entries.title: A formalization of Chang, Liu, and Liu's proof of Chvátal's conjecture

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof that square-difference-free subsets of the polynomials of degree below n over F_3 can be larger than 3^(3n/4). Call A square-difference-free when no two of its elements differ by a nonzero square, and let D_3(n) be the largest size of such a set inside P_{3,n}. A ten-word code S in F_3^4, in which no two words differ by a vector with every coordinate in {0, 1}, drives a lift that carries a square-difference-free subset of P_{3,m} to one of P_{3,m+8} with 810 times as many elements. Iterating it from the bases {0} and B_4 = {a T^3 + b T + c (1 - T^2)} gives square-difference-free sets of size 810^e in degree below 8e and 27 * 810^e in degree below 8e + 4, so the conjectured bound 3^(3n/4) fails at every n divisible by 4 with n >= 8, and 16/21 <= liminf log D_3(n) / (n log 3).
entries.title: ns-lean: Naslund's Conjecture 13 is false at q = 3, k = 2, for every n congruent to 0 mod 4 with n >= 8

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of the core results of "Chain bounding, the leanest proof of Zorn's lemma, and an illustration of computerized proof formalization" by Guillermo L. Incatasciato and Pedro Sánchez Terraf, published at the American Mathematical Monthly (preprint freely accessible at http://arxiv.org/abs/2404.11638). It formalizes the order-theoretic notion of _good chains_ for an "expander" of subsets of a poset: the comparability of good chains, the existence of a greatest good chain, the well-ordering of good chains for an expander of the form C ↦ C ∪ {f C}, the Chain Bounding Lemma (there is no assignment of a strict upper bound to every chain of a poset), the Unbounded Chain Lemma, and — as a novel, unified alternative to the classical ordinal-based arguments — derivations of both Zorn's Lemma and the Bourbaki–Witt fixed point theorem from Chain Bounding.
entries.title: Chain Bounding

entries.abstract: Machine-checked Lean 4 proofs of two theorems about the classical inflation hierarchy. The headline theorem, TriangleInflation.Graph.classification_NW, classifies the scenarios on which the hierarchy terminates: for a pair-source scenario with binary observations, some finite Navascués–Wolfe order characterizes compatibility iff every connected component is a double-star, and then order two suffices. A pair-source scenario is a finite simple graph without isolated vertices, one binary observed variable per vertex and one independent latent source per edge; a double-star is a tree of diameter at most three. The terminating half first labels each component from its graph structure alone: its vertices of degree at least two are pairwise adjacent and number at most two; with two of them they are the centres, with one of them (a star) a neighbour is promoted to the second centre, with none (a single edge) both endpoints are the centres, and every other vertex is a leaf attached to one centre. It then reconstructs a model from any order-two witness: source-disjoint blocks are independent under the witness, and conditioning on a leaf pattern reads off the joint law of the two centres' response tables, which becomes the law of a fresh central source. The nonterminating half supplies, at every order t, a strictly positive law that passes the order-t test and has no model. On an induced cycle the law is the parity target with correlation 1/(4 m^2 t^2), whose witness is a positive Fourier density on m t auxiliary signs pushed forward along products of adjacent signs; its incompatibility is parity rigidity. On an induced five-observer path the law is a bilocal target with h = 1/(16 t^2), whose witness is the inflated law of a pair-source model with complex source weights (1 ± i s/(4t))/4 on the two inner sources, under which the copies are independent and identically distributed; the real part of that law is shown nonnegative by a telescoped triangle inequality, and the incompatibility is the bilocal inequality sqrt|I| + sqrt|J| ≤ 1. Both witnesses are moved to the ambient graph by induced-subgraph transport and made strictly positive by independent local flips. The same development proves the classification for the ancestral-independence and recursively expressible hierarchies, and proves that the latter two coincide on every pair-source scenario. The second theorem, TriangleInflation.no_finite_characterizing_order, is the triangle case made quantitative: for every order t ≥ 1 there is an explicit rational three-bit law that is feasible at order t for the ancestral-independence hierarchy I^AI_t, hence for the Navascués–Wolfe hierarchy I^NW_t, and is not triangle compatible. This answers, in the negative for the triangle, the question Navascués and Wolfe (2020, §4.1) raise about whether some finite order settles exact compatibility; their hierarchy is asymptotically complete, so each incompatible law is rejected at some finite order, but the rejecting order cannot be bounded uniformly. The witnesses are P_t = Q(ε_t, r_t) with ε_t = 1/(2t³) and r_t = (1 − ε_t)^(t−1), where Q(ε,r) = ε δ_000 + (1 − ε) Bern(r)^⊗3. Membership is proved by an explicit inflation law on the order-t copied observations: independent Bernoulli defect bits on the cube [t]³ of source-copy indices together with independent private bits, with an observation outputting 1 exactly when its private bit and every defect on its line vanish. That law is S_t³-symmetric, has the tensor power P^⊗t as its diagonal law, and satisfies the injectable-marginal and ancestral-independence prescriptions. Incompatibility comes from the Finner inequality P(000)² ≤ P_A(0) P_B(0) P_C(0), which P_t violates by at least ε_t²/2 > 0; the inequality is proved both for finite latent alphabets and, in FinnerMeasure.lean, for arbitrary measurable latent spaces. The library also formalizes the order-t fan inequalities and their rejecting-order corollary, the family R_p with rejecting order 2 at every distance, the finite bounds on the first rejecting order along P_ε behind its Θ(ε^{-1/3}) growth, the order-t second-moment rate bound and its convex-order sharpening, the quantitative parity rigidity behind the cycle distance bound, and the square and triangle witnesses at q = 1/(16t). The two registry statements in Palomar/TriangleInflation/ import Mathlib alone and carry their definitions verbatim from TriangleInflation/Defs.lean and TriangleInflation/Graph/Defs.lean.
entries.title: Termination of the classical inflation hierarchy on pair-source networks

entries.abstract: Machine-checked Lean 4 presentation of the four headline theorem families in Section 2 of Davis and Kahan (1970): sin-Theta, tan-Theta, sin-2-Theta, and tan-2-Theta. The Palomar Comparator exposes five selected source-facing declarations: the residual sin-Theta estimate, the residual tan-Theta estimate, both the residual and whole-space sin-2-Theta estimates, and the residual tan-2-Theta estimate. The statements retain the paper's standing separable ambient Hilbert-space scope, permit finite or infinite ambient dimension, and are generic over RCLike scalars to cover the real and complex cases. Their norm quantifier is presented in the Challenge by a dimension-coherent symmetric norming function; the included formalization proves via Fan dominance that the corresponding inequalities yield the source-facing universal unitarily invariant norm estimates.
entries.title: Davis-Kahan 1970: the four Section 2 rotation-of-eigenvectors theorem families

entries.abstract:
In 1926, Fatou conjectured that the Julia set of the complex exponential map is the entire complex plane; in other words, the dynamical system described by the map is unstable under perturbation at every point in the plane.  Misiurewicz proved this conjecture in 1981. In 2015, Shen and Rempe published "The Exponential Map Is Chaotic: An Invitation to Transcendental Dynamics", giving an elementary and conceptual proof of Misiurewicz's theorem and deriving its dynamical consequences, without requiring advanced results  from complex analysis or dynamics.
This project formalises these results in Lean 4: density of escaping points, points with dense orbits, and repelling periodic points; eventual covering of compact subsets of the punctured plane; Devaney chaos; spherical non-equicontinuity; and the fact that the Julia set is the whole complex plane.
entries.title: The exponential map is chaotic

entries.abstract:
Three theorems about binary channels on a doubly symmetric binary source: a pair (𝑋, 𝑌) of
Bernoulli(1/2) bits with P(𝑋 ≠ 𝑌) = 𝑝, together with Markov chains 𝑈 - 𝑋 - 𝑌 - 𝑉 in which 𝑈
and 𝑉 are the outputs of two independent binary channels applied to 𝑋 and to 𝑌. Let 𝒜 be the
set of rate triples (𝑅₀, 𝑅₁, 𝑅₂) with 𝐼(𝑈;𝑋) ≤ 𝑅₁, 𝐼(𝑌;𝑉) ≤ 𝑅₂ and 𝑅₀ ≤ 𝐼(𝑈;𝑉) attainable by
arbitrary binary channels on the two sides, and ℬ the same set with both channels restricted
to be binary symmetric.

(1) conv 𝒜 = conv ℬ for every 𝑝 in [0,1]. (2) At 𝑝 = 0, no pair of binary channels whose rates
do not exceed those of the Z-channel with parameter 𝑎 and the S-channel with parameter 𝑑
attains a larger 𝐼(𝑈;𝑉) than that pair does. (3) At 𝑝 = 0, no pair of binary channels whose
rates are at least those of the Z-channels with parameters 𝑎 and 𝑑 attains a smaller 𝐼(𝑈;𝑉)
than that pair does. Here 𝑎, 𝑑 range over (0,1).
entries.title: BSCAveraging

entries.abstract: This is a Lean 4 formalization of norm-variation of multiple ergodic averages for commuting transformations,  including Tao's norm-convergence theorem. At the heart of the argument is an explicit real-variable estimate for twisted multilinear averages. This formalization is based on the blueprint available at arXiv:2608.27321. The statements of the main theorems have been hand-formalized,  while the proof was autoformalized during a one-week period using coding agents under human supervision.  This produced roughly 107k lines of code (excluding comments and blank lines) and includes proofs of several  prerequisite theorems currently not in mathlib such as multilinear complex interpolation,  the Calderón transference principle, and properties of Wiener space functions.
entries.title: Formalization of norm-variation of multiple ergodic averages for commuting transformations

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of continuous-path Markov processes associated with conservative Feller transition semigroups on nonempty locally compact Polish spaces. A uniform Kolmogorov displacement-moment bound yields a unique measurable kernel from each starting point to continuous-path space, with the prescribed finite-dimensional distributions. The library also develops strong Markov properties, generators and resolvents, stopping and killing, and Brownian motion as an example. The existence and uniqueness theorem is independently checked using Audit/ContinuousMarkovProcess/comparator.json.
entries.title: MarkovProcess

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of the coarse-graining approach to quantitative stochastic homogenization of divergence-form elliptic equations: function-space, deterministic, probabilistic, and homogenization-scale theory up to the quenched minimal-scale theorem. The public main result is a uniformly elliptic, isotropic specialization of the quenched homogenization comparison estimate in Armstrong-Kuusi, "Renormalization Group and Elliptic Homogenization in High Contrast" (Inventiones Mathematicae, 2025), independently checked using Audit/QuenchedComparison/comparator.json, together with four further comparator-checked specializations under Audit/.
entries.title: CoarseGraining

entries.abstract: We prove permutation realization for every admissible binary X-ray profile whose rank deviations from the odd staircase lie in [-2, 2], at every order and without a bound on density slack. We also prove the one-sided families with all deviations at least -1 or all deviations at most 1, with at least 2^u realizations, where u counts positive or negative deviations respectively. For n >= 1, if a label multiset L is realizable at order n, then Q(L) = {3, 2n+1} multiset-union (L+2) is realizable at order n+2. If every source label lies in [2, 2n-2], then h(L) <= h(Q(L)), where h counts permutation realizations. Repeated source labels are allowed. A least-order counterexample to the unrestricted conjecture must have first deviation at least 3 or last deviation at most -3. The unrestricted conjecture remains open.
entries.title: Constructive families and an extension theorem for binary permutation X-rays

entries.abstract: Lean formalization of selected results in B. C. Carlson's theory of special functions as complex Dirichlet averages. The registry selection establishes joint entire-parameter continuation of holomorphic averages on convex open scalar domains; joint holomorphy and native-integral agreement for the Gamma-regularized R and L functions on principal slit-node domains; Euler inversion and Euler-Poisson equations; and Gamma-regularized adaptations of both quadratic R transformations for all complex exponent and Dirichlet parameters with positive-real-part unsquared variables. The L function is related to R by exponent differentiation. The repository also supplies Pochhammer, several-complex-variable, simplex-integration, and Dirichlet foundations, which are not separately selected registry claims. This is a snapshot of an ongoing development, not complete coverage of Carlson's 1977 book or 1987 L-function article.
entries.title: B. C. Carlson's approach to special functions of applied mathematics

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, against Mathlib, of the qualitative statement of J. H. Bae, "A resolution of Erdős Problem #190: the canonical van der Waerden number satisfies H(k)^{1/k}/k → ∞" (arXiv:2604.20588, v2), Corollary 1.2, via the elementary argument of its Section 4.3.  Let H(k) be the least N such that every finite colouring of {1,…,N} contains a monochromatic or a rainbow k-term arithmetic progression; Erdős and Graham (1979) asked whether H(k)^{1/k}/k → ∞ (Problem 190 in Bloom's database).  The compared theorems state that for every C there is K such that for all k ≥ K every N for which [N] is canonical for k satisfies (Ck)^k < N (divergence, and its Filter.Eventually form); this is a statement about canonical N only and by itself says nothing about H(k) (it holds vacuously for a k with no canonical N, where H(k) = sInf ∅ = 0).  Combined with the existence of a canonical N for every k — the Erdős–Graham theorem, via Szemerédi's theorem, which is not formalized — it gives H(k) > (Ck)^k for all large k, i.e. H(k)^{1/k}/k → ∞; that conditional conclusion is stated as H_divergence, with the existence as an explicit hypothesis on H(k) = sInf {N | canonical}.  The fourth compared theorem is the explicit bound behind the argument: for k ≥ 12 there is a prime p with (k−1)/2 < p ≤ k−1 such that every canonical N exceeds p^(p − ⌊k/3⌋)·⌊⌊k/3⌋^(k−1)/(16k²)⌋ (integer divisions, as in the Lean statement).  The proof composes the Erdős–Lovász lower bound W(r,k) − 1 ≥ r^(k−1)/(16k²) for van der Waerden numbers (obtained from the symmetric Lovász local lemma, applied with a number of colours r₀ = ⌊k/3⌋ growing with k), the restricted Blankenship–Cummings–Taranchuk recurrence W(r,k) − 1 ≥ p·(W(r−1,k) − 1) for primes r ≤ p ≤ k, Bertrand's postulate, and elementary asymptotics.  The paper's main theorem, the explicit rate H(k)^{1/k}/k ≥ (1/e − ε(k))·k/log k obtained with the Baker–Harman–Pintz prime-gap theorem, is not formalized (that theorem is not available in Mathlib); the formalized argument gives the weaker rate k^{1/6−o(1)}, which suffices for the qualitative statement.  The compared theorems depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: Erdős Problem 190: every canonical N exceeds (Ck)^k for large k, and H(k)^{1/k}/k → ∞ under the existence hypothesis — a Lean 4 formalization of the qualitative statement of arXiv:2604.20588

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of the fixed-rank asymptotic count for integral matrices over a number field and the convergence of moments of lifts of algebraic codes. The public results preserve the submission PDF's main scale, error terms, echelon-integral limit, and denominator normalization. The intermediate-rank height-counting input attributed to Schmidt is an explicit hypothesis; it is not silently assumed as an axiom.
entries.title: Integral Matrices of Fixed Rank over Number Fields: Lean formalization

entries.abstract: This Lean 4 formalization proves the two main theorems of the paper 'Boundary regularity for non-local operators with symmetric kernels and vanishing horizon' (arXiv:2504.00567v1). For a fractional order s in (1/2,1), the paper studies a nonlocal operator with symmetric kernel whose interaction horizon depends on the distance to the boundary and on a horizon parameter sigma in (0,1], and shrinks near the boundary. The formalization proves that weak solutions u to the Dirichlet problem with zero Dirichlet data and bounded right-hand side are in the Hölder space C^{2s-1} up to the boundary. Furthermore, it is proven that the quotient u/d_Omega^{2s-1} is also Hölder continuous up to the boundary. Both results include norm estimates controlled by the essential supremum of the right-hand side.
entries.title: Boundary regularity for non-local operators with symmetric kernels and vanishing horizon

entries.abstract: For a nonarchimedean local field with residue cardinality q > 2, this development evaluates a sum of three normalized Haar integrals of an explicit eight-term Weyl kernel defined from valuations of entries and two-by-two minors of a concrete 4 by 4 matrix. It proves measurability and Bochner integrability on the natural damped range, an explicit rational evaluation in the undamped interior, principal Abel convergence, and the whole signed special Abel limit at delta = plus or minus q^(-1/2). The Satake parameters are unitary and avoid the stated Weyl walls; the special quotient also excludes parameters equal to its sign. The proof assembles all fifty infinite valuation regions with the source Haar normalizations. This adapts local calculations in Paul, Pitale, Saha and Schmidt's Fourier–Jacobi period paper. Identification of the explicit kernel with the paper's independently defined spherical coefficient and the full period identity are not claimed. The positive special-sign product is identically zero. No undamped special-endpoint integrability or extension to exceptional parameter walls is asserted.
entries.title: Explicit Fourier–Jacobi Haar-core evaluation and Abel limits

entries.abstract:
There are `m` labeled supplies in `[0,1]`. In each period, an independent uniform demand arrives; an online policy selects one live supply, pays the distance between them, and replaces that supply by an independent uniform point. This is the one-dimensional fully dynamic model studied in Kanoria's [*Dynamic spatial matching*](https://doi.org/10.1214/25-AAP2154). That paper established a lower bound of order `log(m)/m` and an upper bound of order `log(m)^2/m`, and posed closing this logarithmic gap as an open problem.

We construct a policy and show that its performance matches the prior known lower bound up to a universal constant factor. Specifically, for every `m >= 2`, from every fixed initial inventory, its root-mean-square one-period cost has limsup at most `C log(m+1)/m`, with `C = 72000/log(2)`. With a scheduled `m`-period replacement phase, its expected average cost, including that phase, has the same bound for every total horizon `N >= 2m^2`. The policy assigns deletion probabilities recursively on a dyadic tree and implements them by quantile transport. Its analysis combines a harmonic inventory potential with a quadratic Bellman inequality. Tree symmetry cancels interactions between spatial scales, while the Bellman inequality controls both transport discrepancy and the curvature loss in the potential drift.
entries.title: A Tight Upper Bound for Fully Dynamic Matching on the Line

entries.abstract: We formalize the boundary of naturality in the labelled conversion calculus of A Theory of a Two-Dimensional Typed Lambda Calculus. Canonical evaluation of inductively presented homotopies constructs naturality squares, and transport along finite presentations preserves two-paths and recovers the naturality boundary. In contrast, an explicit pointwise family on Fin 3 admits no naturality two-cell or finite pasting: a six-element dihedral-group invariant separates its two boundary paths while respecting every declared two-cell generator. This independently reconstructed refutation is classical, not a verification of the manuscript's claimed constructive Idris proof. Supporting results distinguish beta and eta evidence by parity and give a standalone typed de Bruijn syntax with exact raw-tree representation adequacy and a parity-preserving conversion interpretation. The result concerns this declared evidence calculus, not normalization, full abstraction, or a completeness theorem for lambda calculus.
entries.title: Certified naturality and the obstruction to unrestricted naturality in a typed two-dimensional calculus

entries.abstract: We formalize a negative answer to Problem XXII of Schafhauser, Tikuisis and White. There is a separable unital C*-algebra A with nonempty compact tracial state space such that its uniform tracial completion M has a tracial state that is discontinuous in the uniform 2-norm. Thus the canonical extensions of the traces of A form a proper subset X of the traces of M. A second theorem gives a factorial tracially complete pair (M, X) with the same failure, answering Question 1.1 of Carrion, Castillejos, Evington, Gabe, Schafhauser, Tikuisis and White negatively. In both statements, X is exactly the set of uniform-2-norm-continuous traces. The proof uses a unitized c0-sum of antipodally covariant matrix-function algebras of growing rank and dimension. Borsuk-Ulam supplies finite coordinate-state constraints; weak-star compactness produces a corona trace detecting a sequence whose uniform 2-norm tends to zero. Both selected Lean theorems are unconditional. The completion is characterized by tracial completeness, unique restriction of designated traces to all base traces, and density in the uniform 2-norm.
entries.title: A Counterexample to the Trace Problem for Uniform Tracial Completions

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of Guy Robin's 1984 equivalence between the Riemann hypothesis and the strict divisor-sum inequality sigma(n) < exp(gamma) n log(log n) for every integer n > 5040.  The development also proves the restriction to colossally abundant integers, reconstructs the Nicolas--Landau oscillation argument used for the converse implication, and checks the finite ranges with exact Lean certificates.  It also formalizes Lagarias's 2001 elementary harmonic-number criterion and its equivalence to the Riemann hypothesis. This is a formalization of equivalence criteria; it does not prove the Riemann hypothesis.
entries.title: Robin1984

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the MI-32 upper bound, that is, of the Latała-Świątkowski conjecture that for every regularity parameter alpha >= 1 there is a constant C > 0, independent of the dimension and of the entry laws, with E||X|| <= C (M(X) + D(X)) for every square random matrix X with independent mean-zero real entries whose absolute moments satisfy ||X_ij||_{L_2r} <= alpha ||X_ij||_{L_r} at every real order r >= 1. Here ||.|| is the Euclidean operator norm, M(X) is the sum of the largest row and column standard deviations, and D(X) is the max-min weak moment at order log(k+1) taken over one shared deterministic deletion set on both axes. The probability space is arbitrary and the subunit order log 2 at k = 1 is kept literally. The selected theorem MI32.main_upper carries a complete proof whose transitive axiom audit reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The proof runs through original-law positive-polynomial moments and interpolation, exact occupation-count localization, finite nets, a direct independent-coordinate Hilbert comparison, full original-law creator and annihilator contractions, positive vacuum iteration giving the local symmetric-law operator-moment theorem at the exact order log(n+1), a nested deterministic deletion decomposition with cubic two-sided variance screening, an elementary centered-Gram estimate for the far remainder, two two-shell block families controlled by the local theorem at scheduled orders, and the original-copy symmetrization reduction. Constants are explicit and conservative, not optimized.
entries.title: MI-32: Lean formalization of the parity and positive-polynomial upper bound

entries.abstract: We prove sufficient conditions for partitioning the edges of a connected finite simple graph into at most ⌈|V(G)|/2⌉ simple paths. The results concern bowtie components—two triangles sharing exactly one vertex—in the subgraph induced by even-degree vertices. They include removal preserving specified endpoints, a sharp full-incidence star expansion, composition under explicit boundary hypotheses, and corollaries for graphs with two bowtie components. The unrestricted two-exception conjecture remains open.
entries.title: Gallai’s Path Decomposition Conjecture for Graphs with Small Bowtie Boundaries

entries.abstract: This Lean 4 formalization of Kong and Zeng's To cover a permutohedron (arXiv:2509.13877v3, 9 April 2026) determines the minimum number of affine hyperplanes needed to cover the permutation vertices of (1,...,n), excluding the hyperplane containing every vertex. The exact answer is n for odd n at least 3, and n-1 for even n at least 4. It also proves that an arbitrary injective real tuple of length n at least 2 has the sharp hyperplane intersection bound (n-1)! when its n-1 signed critical values are distinct. Genuine polynomial-root path lifting establishes local transpositions and the cycle at infinity, with explicit corrections to the source's loop hypotheses. A symmetric polynomial norm replaces the paper's general Bezout step. One independent Challenge and one Comparator configuration cover all eighteen results, including sharp constructions, generic and four-element consequences, and the connection with convex vertices and arbitrary affine hyperplanes.
entries.title: To cover a permutohedron

entries.abstract: A Lean+mathlib proof of Nivat's conjecture: Given a finite alphabet A, we consider configurations c: Z^2 -> A, which are arbitrary maps that can be thought of as colorings of the 2D lattice. Writing P_c(m, n) for the number of distinct m-by-n block patterns occurring in a configuration c, Nivat conjectured that if P_c(m, n) <= mn for some positive m and n, then c is periodic; that is, there exists nonzero h such that c(v+h) = c(v) for all v. The proof is due to GPT-6 Pro.
entries.title: A proof of Nivat's conjecture

entries.abstract: We formalize the existence of a finitely generated surjunctive group that is not sofic. This answers negatively the converse to the Gromov-Weiss surjunctivity theorem, recorded as open problem OP-11 by Ceccherini-Silberstein and Coornaert and as Problem 1.1 by Bowen and Chapman. The witness is the symmetric double G *_Gamma G, where Gamma = EL_3(F_2[x_1,x_2,x_3]) and G = EL_3(F_2[x_1^+-1,x_2^+-1,x_3^+-1]) semidirect EL_3(Z), with the action given by monomial substitution. Kun and Thom constructed this pair and proved the double nonsofic. The new ingredient here is a surjunctivity theorem for symmetric doubles of surjunctive groups. The Lean development proves both halves for this witness, including the required permutation centralizer normalization theorem. The challenge states surjunctivity through finite-memory cellular automata and soficity through finite normalized-Hamming models. The two selected declarations assert the finitely generated counterexample and the failure of the universal converse.
entries.title: A Surjunctive Group That Is Not Sofic

entries.abstract: Exact height-span of Mazur's scheme grammar, a local dart-mass bound, and an adjugate identity for the Dirichlet matrix of that construction; not a proof of the strong Papadimitriou–Ratajczak conjecture and not a theorem that every 3-connected plane graph attains the scheme maximum. Mazur builds injective integer heights by inductive recurrences on rooted pieces (edge, cycle, binary series, two-range join) and then forms a weighted Dirichlet matrix for the horizontal coordinate; the paper does not bound the height span or the bit length of the coordinates. For a well-formed scheme on n >= 2 vertices with j nontrivial joins, T+1 <= 2^j (n-2j), attained at every admissible pair (n,j)=(2,0) or 2j+3 <= n. The one-parameter maximum is F(n) = 2^{n/2}-1 (n even) or 3 * 2^{(n-3)/2}-1 (n odd). The coarser bound T <= 2^{n-2} remains. An integer matrix has |det| at most the product of its row ell_1-norms. Heights in {0,...,T} force Mazur's interior dart weights to be at most (n-1)T, so every Dirichlet row has ell_1-norm at most 2(n-1)^2 T when T >= 1, and |det M| <= (2(n-1)^2 T)^n; locally the interior outgoing dart-weight sum is at most a_s b_s T. Combining the coarser span bound with the row-sum bound sizes T^2 |det M| and T^2 |det M| T. Independently of invertibility, under the height bound h i <= T, z = adj(M) u satisfies Mz = Delta u and z_s = Delta h_s (T-h_s) on the boundary as ordinary integer subtraction. Polynomial-area Euclidean planar greedy drawings of all 3-connected planar graphs remain open (Da Lozzo–D'Angelo–Frati, COCOON 2020).
entries.title: md-lean: exact height span, dart mass, and adjugate scaling for Mazur's greedy construction

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization proving Dimitrov's Conjectures 1 and 3 for every natural k >= 1 and n >= 2. The results concern inequalities involving Euler's totient, Dedekind's psi function, and the sum-of-divisors function. The source paper proves the k = 1 instances and discusses k = 2, 3; this development covers the full stated range, including k >= 4, and additionally proves for each inequality that equality holds exactly when n is prime. By supplying the full parameter range and sharp equality cases beyond those treated in the source, the project is relevant to researchers in elementary and analytic number theory who study inequalities among multiplicative arithmetic functions, and to formal-mathematics researchers studying the verification of contemporary conjectures. Historical priority for the full-range proofs has not been established by expert or source-author review. The mathematical reductions, Lean code, and documentation were generated substantially by OpenAI Codex under human direction, as detailed below.
entries.title: Lean proofs of Dimitrov's Conjectures 1 and 3

entries.abstract: Brown asks in 2001 (arXiv:math/0111286, Question 11.7) whether an infinite simple discrete group with Kazhdan's property (T) can embed in the unitary group of an R^ω-embeddable McDuff factor, which for such a group is hyperlinearity; Ozawa asks it in 2003 in that language, in About the QWEP conjecture (arXiv:math/0306067); and Pestov prints it, with the sofic form added, as Open question 9.1 of Hyperlinear and sofic groups: a brief guide (arXiv:0804.3968): can an infinite simple group with Kazhdan's property (T) be hyperlinear, or sofic? This project proves, in Lean 4 over Mathlib, that the answer is yes in both forms. The witness is EL₃(A), the group generated by the elementary matrices of size three over the ring A = LC(X, 𝔽₂) ⋊ ℤ, the algebraic crossed product of the locally constant 𝔽₂-valued functions on a binary Toeplitz subshift X by the shift. The ring is finitely generated and simple with center 𝔽₂; the group is infinite and simple, has property (T) by the theorem of Ershov and Jaikin-Zapirain, proved here, and is locally embeddable into finite groups by periodic models of the Toeplitz sequence, so it is sofic and hyperlinear. The two compared theorems state the existence of an infinite simple group with property (T) that is hyperlinear, and of one that is sofic, with property (T), soficity and hyperlinearity defined in the Challenge from the textbook sources; their axiom closure is propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The prose of this submission, this abstract included, was written by Claude (Anthropic).
entries.title: An Infinite Simple Group with Property (T) That Is Sofic and Hyperlinear

entries.abstract: Let J be the split Albert algebra over a field k of characteristic zero, the 27-dimensional Jordan algebra of 3 by 3 Hermitian matrices over the split octonions, with trace tr. A frame is an ordered triple of trace-one idempotents summing to 1. Three frames E, F, K carry 54 natural invariants under the group G of all unital k-linear bijections of J preserving its Jordan product: the pair traces tr(eᵢ∘fⱼ), tr(fⱼ∘kₗ), tr(kₗ∘eᵢ) and the triple traces tr(eᵢ∘(fⱼ∘kₗ)). This Lean 4 development proves that these traces do not generate all rational invariants of three frames, and that adjoining one additional invariant suffices: the field of G-invariant rational functions on the variety of frame triples is a quadratic extension H(d) of the field H generated by the 54 traces, where d = tr(W∘(W∘W)), W = x∘(y∘z) − y∘(x∘z), x = e₂ − e₀, y = f₂ − f₀, z = k₂ − k₀. The development also proves that the variety of frame triples is irreducible, that the coordinate algebra used is the standard split Albert algebra, that d is not in H, and that every invariant is uniquely a + b·d with a, b in H. The ambiguity occurs over ℚ: two explicit frame triples have identical 54 traces and d = −2591357/62208 and −1782559/62208, and no ℚ-linear automorphism of J combined with any of the 1,296 relabellings of frames and idempotents carries one to the other. The proved endpoints use only the permitted axiom dependencies propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice; a Python script rechecks the example in exact arithmetic.
entries.title: Rational invariants of three frames in the split Albert algebra: a Lean formalization

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of Krachun's directed (acyclic-block) lower-bound construction for sets of integers with no k-th-power difference, stated and proved for every exponent k >= 2. Let D_k(N) be the largest size of a subset of {1,...,N} no two of whose elements differ by a nonzero perfect k-th power. A pool for k is a nonempty list of blocks (m, sup, H) with pairwise coprime square-free moduli m >= 2, heights H >= 2, and sup a nonempty list of (vertex, rank) pairs with distinct vertices below m, ranks below H, and a strict rank drop along every ordered pair of vertices whose difference is a nonzero k-th-power residue mod m (so the induced digraph is acyclic). For every such pool, alpha k P <= liminf log D_k(N)/log N, where alpha k P = (sum ((k-1) log m + log t)/log H) / (1 + k sum log m / log H) and t >= 1 is the number of vertices of a block; and N^rho <= D_k(N) for all large N whenever rho < alpha k P. The theorem is instantiated at k = 4 with nine blocks, eight on the primes 5, 13, 29, 37, 53, 61, 101, 109 and one at the composite square-free modulus 51 = 3 * 17, and at k = 6 with nine blocks on the primes 7, 19, 31, 43, 67, 79, 103, 127, 139, giving the exponents 0.912145042700... and 0.950825559086..., each proved to exceed the corresponding Ruzsa transfer value ((3 + log 6/log 17)/4 = 0.908103119289... and (5 + log 6/log 13)/6 = 0.949759249243..., the latter being Ruzsa's own published Corollary at k = 6) and the decimal bounds 0.9121 and 0.9508, by exact comparisons of natural powers.
entries.title: rk-lean: the directed construction for k-th-power-difference-free sets at every k, with the exponents 0.912145 (k = 4) and 0.950826 (k = 6)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of the second paper on the sets Z_{p/q}(s, s+t) = {ξ > 0 : {ξ(p/q)ⁿ} ∈ [s, s+t) for all n ≥ 0}, the generalized Z-numbers of Flatto, Lagarias and Pollington. The first paper built a corpus of block certificates for individual statements Z_{p/q}(U) = ∅. This paper replaces parts of that corpus by theorems, and then asks what the certificate format can and cannot reach. Thirty certificates in the regime p > q² collapse into one closed-form criterion on the single real parameter ε = {(p−q)s}, settling a set of positions of measure 1 − 2q²/(p(p+q)) at every base and for every real ξ ≠ 0; the criterion extends to a family indexed by a depth K, identified with the finiteness criterion of [FLP95] and with the parameter intervals J¹_b of [Bug04], the depth playing the role of the denominator of the rotation number. An explicit escape time for L ≤ ξ ≤ X is extracted from the soundness proof, and every unranked certificate of [Ste26] is made effective by it. A completeness theorem says the verdict is forced on the class where a certificate can exist — a finite hold set — and that an infinite hold set refuses every unranked certificate at every depth and over every denominator, which turns a bounded computer search into a theorem. A measure-theoretic depth–size bound 1 ≤ 2δ(K + 2 + log_{p/q} 2B) prices [KK17, Prob. 6.1] for this format. Finally a rank-stratified certificate gives ‖ξ(3/2)ⁿ‖ < 2/7 = 0.285714… infinitely often for every ξ ≠ 0, past the 31/81 = 0.38271… of [Dub19] as a window and past the corpus's own 1/3 as a nearest-integer constant.
entries.title: Confinement schemas and the reach of block certificates for powers of rational numbers modulo one

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of the Broughton--Huff theorem that the ordinary union of a strictly increasing sequence of sigma-fields is not a sigma-field. The proof also proves the existence of a set measurable in the lattice supremum but in none of the individual sigma-fields.
entries.title: The Broughton--Huff theorem on increasing unions of sigma-fields

entries.abstract: Formalizes in Lean 4 the resolution of a 2019 OEIS conjecture of L. H. Gallardo (comment on A071642; TheoremDB P12771): for every n ≥ 2 the all-ones polynomial 1 + X + ⋯ + Xⁿ is irreducible over GF(2) if and only if 1 + P + ⋯ + Pⁿ is irreducible over GF(2), where P = X² + X + 1. The compared statements are the per-n equivalence, the literal set-level form of the OEIS comment (the terms ≥ 2 coincide), and the failure of the excluded case n = 1. The proof is elementary: a factorization of the all-ones polynomial composes to one of the substituted polynomial; conversely irreducibility forces n even, the X^(n-1) coefficient gives trace 1 for a root α, hence Tr(α + 1) = 1, so Z² + Z + (α + 1) has no root in GF(2^n) (Frobenius-invariance of the trace), a root β of it satisfies P(β) = α and has degree 2n, and the monic degree-2n polynomial 1 + P + ⋯ + Pⁿ vanishing at β is its minimal polynomial. SCOPE. The full conjecture is formalized with no weakened hypothesis. NOT CLAIMED: novelty of the mechanism, which is the classical trace criterion for compositions f(X² + X + c) over binary fields (Varshamov 1984, Meyn 1990); the contribution is the resolution of the specific OEIS conjecture and its machine check. AUDIENCE: finite fields and integer sequences.
entries.title: All-ones polynomials over GF(2) under the substitution X ↦ X² + X + 1 (OEIS A071642, TheoremDB P12771)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of Younis's lower-bound construction for subsets of {1,...,N} with no configuration {x, x+y, x+y^2} (y nonzero), in its two-set form: for every square-free modulus m and residue sets R1, R2 modulo m with R1 square-difference-free and no nonzero difference of R2 equal to the square of a difference of R1, the interval {1,...,N} contains a configuration-free set of size at least C(rho) N^rho for every rho below 1/2 + log|R1|/(3 log m) + log|R2|/(6 log m). The theorem is instantiated at m = 145 with |R1| = 10 and |R2| = 32, giving the exponent 0.770287..., which is proved to exceed Younis's exponent 0.768503... (m = 65, sizes 7 and 17) by exact comparisons of integer powers; decimal bounds 0.7702 < gamma < 0.77029 are also proved, and the bound is stated in liminf form for the counting function D(N).
entries.title: ry-lean: sets avoiding {x, x+y, x+y²} — Younis's two-set construction and the exponent 0.77028
